definition_zh: 单脚跳；蹦跳；跳过；跳上；短途旅行
definition_en: to jump on one leg or with both feet together, to move quickly by such jumps, or a short jump or journey
core_image: 一只麻雀收拢双脚，一下子蹦到下一根树枝上
scene: 公园的长椅上落着一只麻雀，人一走近它就一蹦一蹦地挪开。A robin hops across the wet lawn looking for worms.
sceneCN: 这里 hop 是「蹦跳」（第 1 个义项：单脚或双脚并拢连续短跳）；句意：一只知更鸟在湿漉漉的草坪上蹦跳着找虫吃。图中可辨识物件：麻雀、长椅、湿草坪。

derivatives.zh: 由 hop 加 -er 构成，义为「单脚跳的人或物」，也指蹦跳着走的昆虫
由现在分词转为形容词，义为「热闹忙碌的；蹦跳的」
由啤酒花词义的 hop 加 picker 构成，义为「啤酒花采摘工」，是另一条同形来源
由 grass 与 hopper 复合而成，义为「蚱蜢」，把「蹦跳者」的意象带进复合词

senses.title: To jump on one leg
senses.definition: to move by jumping on one leg, or to make short jumps with both feet together
senses.definitionCN: 单脚跳跃前进，或双脚并拢做短距离的跳跃
senses.example: The children hopped from one square to the next.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们从一个格子里跳到下一个格子里。
senses.why: The word imitates a short light jump, and the earliest picture is a body lifting briefly off the ground; a bird or a child with legs joined gives the base sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词模仿的是一种轻快的短跳，最早的画面是身体短暂离开地面；鸟类或双腿并拢的孩子正好给出来最基础的义项。

senses.title: To move quickly by jumps
senses.definition: to move somewhere quickly in short jumps rather than walking steadily
senses.definitionCN: 以短距离跳跃而非平稳走路的方式快速移动
senses.example: The rabbit hopped across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 兔子蹦跳着穿过田野。
senses.why: Since each jump covers little ground, many jumps in a row become a way of travelling, so hop grows into a manner of moving quickly.
senses.whyCN: 每一次跳都只能挪一小段，连起来就成了一种前进方式，于是 hop 扩展为「快速移动的姿态」。

senses.title: To get on and off quickly
senses.definition: to get on, off or into a vehicle quickly and without ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 迅速、不拘礼节地上下车或进入交通工具
senses.example: We hopped on the first train we saw.
senses.exampleCN: 我们跳上了看到的第一班火车。
senses.why: A light jump is exactly what boarding a bus or train feels like, so hop becomes the informal verb for a quick entry or exit.
senses.whyCN: 上公交、上火车的感觉正像一次轻跳，所以 hop 也成了表示迅速上下车的口语动词。

senses.title: To cross over something
senses.definition: to jump over something, especially something low such as a ditch, fence or border
senses.definitionCN: 跃过某物，尤指沟渠、栅栏或边界这类低矮之物
senses.example: He hopped the fence and ran down the lane.
senses.exampleCN: 他跳过栅栏，沿着小路跑去。
senses.why: If a jump clears a height, the thing underneath is passed over; hop therefore takes an object and means to jump across it.
senses.whyCN: 一次跳越若跨过了高度，下面的东西就被越过；于是 hop 也能带宾语，表示「跳过去」。

senses.title: A short journey
senses.definition: a short trip, usually informal and often by plane or train
senses.definitionCN: 一次短途出行，通常随意，多坐飞机或火车
senses.example: The island is a short hop from the mainland.
senses.exampleCN: 从大陆到这座岛是一段很短的航程。
senses.why: A journey made of short jumps is a journey that is itself short, so the noun hop turns a light leap into a light trip.
senses.whyCN: 由一段段短跳组成的路程，本身也是一段短途；于是名词 hop 把「轻跳」变成「轻装出行」。

intro.en: Hop is a native English word formed by imitating a short light jump; it is not related to the formal word hop meaning the climbing plant.
intro.cn: hop 是英语本族词，由模仿轻快短跳的声音与动作而来；它与表示「啤酒花」的词形相同，但来源不同。

items.en: The verb hoppian is recorded in Old English meaning to leap or dance, so the word is native rather than borrowed.
items.cn: 古英语中已有动词 hoppian，意为「跳跃、跳舞」，说明这个词是本族词而非外来借词。

items.en: A common Germanic form is reconstructed for the family, and the word is generally described as imitative of a quick, light movement; the exact older form is not certain.
items.cn: 这一词族可重构出一个日耳曼语共同形式，一般认为它模仿快速轻巧的动作；更早的确切形式不确定。

items.en: Middle English hopien and hoppen keep the jumping sense, and the noun hop appears alongside the verb.
items.cn: 中古英语的 hopien 与 hoppen 保留跳跃义，名词 hop 也与动词并行出现。

items.en: Hop on and off begin to describe quick boarding, and hop extends to crossing a fence or a border.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，hop on 与 hop off 开始表示迅速上下车，hop 也扩展为「跳过栅栏或边界」。

items.en: A short hop becomes a short trip, especially by air, and hop turns up in phrases such as hop on a bus or a hop across the Channel.
items.cn: a short hop 变成「一段短途旅行」，尤其指空中行程；hop 也出现在「跳上公交」「跨过海峡」这类说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share the same short jump or merely look close to hop; the near-meaning group gathers the other jump verbs with different force and direction.
note.cn: 形近组收同样表示短跳、或只是拼写相近的词；近义组收其他跳跃动词，区别在于力度与方向。

entries.definition: One who hops, or a container that feeds material; formed directly from hop with -er.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蹦跳者」或「料斗」，由 hop 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A person who picks hops, the flowers used in beer; this hop is a different word, though it is spelled the same.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「啤酒花采摘工」，这里的 hop 指啤酒花，虽然拼写相同，词源不同。

entries.definition: A children game of hopping over numbered squares; the first part is our hop.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「跳房子」，孩童按格号单脚跳的游戏，前半部分正是 hop。

entries.definition: To push off the ground with both feet; the general and strongest verb, wider than hop.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「跳、跳跃」，最通用也最有力，范围比 hop 更宽。

entries.definition: To jump a long way or over a gap; more dramatic and longer than hop.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「跃过、腾跃」，比 hop 更有戏剧性、距离更长。

entries.definition: To move with light alternate hops and steps, or to leave something out.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「轻快地交替蹦跳」，也表示「略过」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English form and the everyday phrases that hop appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语词形，以及 hop 实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Old English already had hoppian for jumping and dancing, so hop is an old native word.
normal.cn: 古英语里已有表示跳跃、跳舞的 hoppian，所以 hop 是很古老的本族词。

normal.en: Like other short words that copy an action, hop sounds like the little jump it names.
normal.cn: 像其他模拟动作的短词一样，hop 的读音就带着那一小跳的轻快。

normal.en: Hop on a bus puts the light jump onto a vehicle, and the phrase needs no article before bus.
normal.cn: hop on a bus 把轻跳移到车上，这个说法里 bus 前仍用不定冠词。

normal.en: Past and participle double the p: hopped, hopped, hopping.
normal.cn: 过去式与过去分词都要双写 p：hopped、hopped、hopping。

normal.en: A short hop is a short trip, often by plane or train.
normal.cn: a short hop 指一段短途行程，多坐飞机或火车。

abstract.en: Picture a sparrow settling on a bush, then one small pushing and it is on the next branch.
abstract.cn: 想象一只麻雀落在树丛上，轻轻一蹬，就到了下一根枝条。

abstract.en: Picture a rabbit crossing a field: the journey is just the jumps arriving one after another.
abstract.cn: 想象一只兔子穿过田野：整段路程不过是一次次跳跃接续着到来。

abstract.en: Picture the same small jump directed at a bus door, and the leap becomes boarding.
abstract.cn: 想象同样那一小跳朝着车门跳去，跳跃就变成了上车。

examples.en: The sparrow hopped onto the fence and watched us.
examples.cn: 麻雀跳上栅栏，看着我们。

examples.en: We hopped on a bus and went to the coast for the day.
examples.cn: 我们跳上公交车，去海边玩了一天。

examples.en: It is only a short hop by train from here.
examples.cn: 从这里坐火车过去只是一段很短的路程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「好泼」——雨天路上一个水坑，好泼溅地蹦着跳过，正是蹦跳；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 hoppian「跳跃、跳舞」，一般认为模仿轻快的短跳动作（更早的日耳曼语共同形式为重构，来源不完全确定）；核心义「短暂离地的一小跳」，后扩展出「上下车」「跳过」「短途行程」。

sensesIntro.en: Hop starts from a light short jump, then turns into a way of travelling, then a way of getting on and off, then of clearing an obstacle, and finally a short trip.
sensesIntro.cn: hop 从「轻快的一小跳」出发，扩展为一种移动方式、上下车的动作、越过障碍，最后成为「一小段旅程」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bird lifts off and lands a short way ahead.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只鸟轻轻离地，落在前方不远处。

branches.en: THE BODY: one leg or two feet pushing off the ground is the base picture.
branches.cn: 身体线：单腿或双脚蹬地离位，是最基础的画面。

branches.en: THE MOTION: a row of small jumps becomes a way of crossing space.
branches.cn: 移动线：一连串小跳构成穿过空间的方式。

branches.en: THE VEHICLE: the same light jump now lands you inside a bus or train.
branches.cn: 交通线：同样那一小跳，落在车门或车厢里。

branches.en: THE OBSTACLE: a jump can target a height, so hop takes an object and means to clear it.
branches.cn: 障碍线：跳跃可以瞄准高度，于是 hop 带宾语表示「越过」。

branches.en: THE JOURNEY: a trip made of short jumps is itself short, hence a short hop.
branches.cn: 旅程线：由短跳构成的行程本身也短，于是有了 a short hop。

intro.en: Hop is a native verb that takes ordinary English suffixes; unlike borrowing words, it has no Latin prefix to build on.
intro.cn: hop 是本族动词，只加英语常见的后缀；与外来的借词不同，它没有可拆解的拉丁语前缀。

latinIntro.en: Hop has no Latin origin, so the related forms below are English suffixes and compounds rather than Latin elements.
latinIntro.cn: hop 没有拉丁语来源，下面列出的都是英语后缀与复合词，而不是拉丁语成分。

items.example: Hoppian is the oldest recorded form of hop.
items.exampleCN: hoppian 是 hop 最早有记录的词形。

items.example: Hop keeps the base jumping sense.
items.exampleCN: hop 保留动词的「跳」义。

items.example: The suffix -er forms hopper.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 hopper。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms hopping.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 hopping。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms hopped.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 hopped。

items.example: The suffix -y forms hoppy, used informally.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成口语用的 hoppy。

items.example: Grass combines with hopper to make grasshopper.
items.exampleCN: grass 与 hopper 复合成 grasshopper。

items.example: Grasshopper keeps the picture of a jumper.
items.exampleCN: grasshopper 保留「跳跃者」的画面。

definition_zh: 一大群（人）；游牧部落；人群一拥而上
definition_en: a very large group of people that moves together, often in a disorderly or threatening way
core_image: 草原上密密麻麻的骑兵与家属连成一片，朝同一方向滚滚移动
scene: 周末的商场挤满了人，黑压压地涌向打折柜台。At the weekend sale a horde of shoppers poured towards the discount counter.
sceneCN: 这里 horde 是「一大群人」（第 1 个义项：成群结队、规模浩大移动的人群）；句意：周末的商场挤满了人，黑压压地涌向打折柜台。

pos.zh: 成群结队地涌去（多见于英式用法）

collocations.zh: 成群涌进（英式动作用法）

derivatives.zh: 由单数加 -s 构成的复数，最常与 of 连用表示「成群的……」
horde 的动作用法 + in（进入），义为「成群涌入」，多见于英式英语
horde（人群）+ -like（像……的），义为「像人群涌来那样密集的」，属少见临时组合

senses.title: A very large moving crowd
senses.titleCN: 一大群人；成群结队的人
senses.definition: a great number of people moving or gathering together, usually in a way that feels overwhelming or disorderly
senses.definitionCN: 数量很大、一起移动或聚集的人，常带有难以招架或杂乱无序的感觉
senses.example: Hordes of fans waited outside the stadium.
senses.exampleCN: 成群成群的球迷等在体育场外面。
senses.why: The word began as a label for a whole wandering camp, so any crowd that moves as one mass can now be called a horde.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指整个流动的营地，因此任何作为一个整体移动的人群都可以叫 horde，核心仍是「连成一个团块地移动」。

senses.title: A nomadic people on the move
senses.definition: a group of nomadic people who roam and migrate together with their animals and families
senses.definitionCN: 带着牲畜和家眷一起漫游、迁徙的游牧人群
senses.example: A horde of horsemen crossed the steppe each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 每年春天，都有一支游牧骑兵穿越草原。
senses.why: In its old Turkish form the word named the ruler's camp and the people gathered around it, so it naturally described nomadic nations rather than mere counts of people.
senses.whyCN: 在突厥语原形中，这个词指首领的营帳与聚在其周围的人，所以它天然指向游牧部族这一整体，而不只是数人头。

senses.title: A crowd pouring forward together
senses.definition: to move somewhere as a large crowd and hurry into a place (chiefly British usage)
senses.definitionCN: 像大群那样一窝蜂地移动、挤进某处（主要为英式用法）
senses.example: The children horde into the shop when the sweets arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 糖果一到货，孩子们就成群挤进小店。
senses.why: Once a noun for a mass of people, the word could be turned into a verb for the very act of pouring forward as that mass.
senses.whyCN: 名词既然表示一整团人群，就可以顺势动词化，表示「像那团人群一样向前涌」的动作。

senses.title: A pack of insects or animals
senses.definition: a large number of insects or other animals occurring or moving together
senses.definitionCN: 数量很大、一起出现或移动的昆虫或其他动物
senses.example: A horde of insects settled on the crops.
senses.exampleCN: 一大群昆虫落在庄稼上。
senses.why: The threatening sense of a massed human crowd was transferred to animals that arrive in overwhelming numbers.
senses.whyCN: 人类人群「来势汹汹」的意味被转借给昆虫和动物，凡是铺天盖地地出现，都可以用 horde。

senses.title: A great number of things
senses.definition: a large amount of something seen as an overwhelming mass, often in informal writing
senses.definitionCN: 被视为压倒性的一大堆某物，多用于非正式写作
senses.example: Hordes of emails piled up while she was away.
senses.exampleCN: 她出门期间，邮件堆了一大堆。
senses.why: Once horde stopped counting people only, it could describe any mass that piles up faster than one can handle.
senses.whyCN: 当 horde 不再只数人时，它也用来形容以处理不过来的速度堆积起来的任何东西。

intro.en: Horde is a Turkic word for a camp or a band of warriors that travelled with a ruler; it entered European languages mainly through Polish and French in the sixteenth century, and its spelling has varied ever since.
intro.cn: horde 源出突厥语中指营地、或指随首领行动的队伍的词；16 世纪主要经波兰语和法语进入欧洲语言，拼写此后一直不统一。

items.en: Ordu meant a camp, an army, or the headquarters of a ruler, and related forms in Turkic languages later named the mobile court and household of a chieftain.
items.cn: ordu 意为营地、军队或君主的驻地；突厥语中相关同族形式后来指首领流动的宫帐与眷属。

items.en: Through the golden-horde powers of the steppe the word passed into Russian as orda, and into medieval Latin and Polish as horda, naming the camps of Mongol and Tatar armies.
items.cn: 经由草原上的金帐汗国，这个词进入俄语作 orda、进入中古拉丁语与波兰语作 horda，用来指蒙古与鞑靼军队的营地。

items.en: English borrowed the word from Polish and French sources in the sixteenth century; the spelling wavered between horde and hord before horde settled.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪从波兰语与法语渠道借入这个词，拼写在 horde 与 hord 之间摇摆，最后固定为 horde。

items.en: Early English use described Tatar and Turkish armies moving together with families and animals, which explains the lasting sense of a people on the march.
items.cn: 早期英语用它描写随家眷牲畜一起移动的鞑靼与土耳其军队，这解释了「整体在行进的部族」这一持久义项。

items.en: In later use horde spread to any disorderly crowd, packs of insects, and a British verb meaning to swarm into a place.
items.cn: 在后来的用法中，horde 扩展到任何乱哄哄的人群、成群的昆虫，以及在英式英语中表示「蜂拥而入」的动词。

note.en: Horde sits among crowd words such as mob and swarm, and is easily confused in spelling with hoard, a store kept in secret.
note.cn: horde 与 mob、swarm 这类人群或虫群的词相邻，拼写上也容易与表示秘诀收藏的 hoard 混淆。

entries.definition: a secret store of money or goods; to store things up
entries.definitionCN: 暗藏的财物；囤积。与 horde 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: excrement or filth
entries.definitionCN: 粪便；污物。与 horde 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the arrangement of things or a command
entries.definitionCN: 顺序；命令。与突厥语来源的 horde 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a large number of people gathered in one place
entries.definitionCN: 人群；拥挤；一群人

entries.definition: a large, disorderly and often violent crowd
entries.definitionCN: 暴民；乱哄哄的一群人

entries.definition: a very large number of insects or people moving in one mass
entries.definitionCN: 一群（蜂等）；蜂拥的人潮

normalIntro.en: Horde is a Turkic camp word that travelled west through Polish and French; at heart it is a whole moving camp, not just a number of people.
normalIntro.cn: horde 是源自突厥语的「营地」词，经波兰语和法语向西传；它的核心是整座移动的营地，而不只是一个人数。

normal.en: Keep the silent e: horde is a crowd, hoard is a hidden store.
normal.cn: 看清词尾那个不发音的 e：horde 是人群，hoard 是暗藏的财物。

normal.en: Attack in hordes is a fixed phrase for a mass rush.
normal.cn: attack in hordes 是固定说法，表示成群猛扑而来。

normal.en: Hordes of tourists arrive every July.
normal.cn: 每年七月都有成群的游客到来。

normal.en: In the steppe nations, a horde was the ruler and all who moved with him.
normal.cn: 在草原民族中，horde 指首领与他所率领的所有随行之人。

normal.en: Compare crowd: a crowd gathers, while a horde moves as one mass and often sounds threatening.
normal.cn: 对比 crowd：crowd 是聚在一起，horde 是像一整团那样移动，且常带威胁感。

abstract.en: Picture a tide of riders, carts and animals crossing the plain in a single dark band.
abstract.cn: 想象一片骑手、车马和牲畜汇成深色长带，横穿平原。

abstract.en: See a wall of tents on the move, each family carrying its life on a cart.
abstract.cn: 想象会移动的帐篷之墙，每户人家都用一辆车带着全部家当。

abstract.en: Feel the floor tremble as a crowd pours through a doorway like sand from a bag.
abstract.cn: 感受人群像袋里的沙子一样挤过门口时地面微微震动。

examples.en: Hordes of visitors flooded the old town on the first warm day of spring.
examples.cn: 春天第一个暖日，成群成群的游客涌进老城。

examples.en: Historians describe the horde as a moving camp rather than a simple army.
examples.cn: 历史学家把这个游牧部落描述为一座移动的营地，而不只是一支军队。

examples.en: A few activists changed the policy, not a faceless horde of strangers.
examples.cn: 改变政策的是少数活动人士，而不是一大群面目模糊的陌生人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吼的」——人一多就吵吵嚷嚷、一路吼着过来，一大群人的阵仗；这只是谐音联想，与突厥语词源无关。

root: 突厥语 ordu（营地、军队、首领驻地）→ 鞑靼语/俄语 orda、波兰语 horda → 欧洲语言 → 古法语 horde → 英语 horde，核心义「整座人畜一同移动的营地」。

sensesIntro.en: Horde begins with a wandering camp of nomads, becomes a threatening moving crowd, then a verb for swarming in, and finally any overwhelming mass of insects or things.
sensesIntro.cn: horde 先指游牧的流动营地，再指来势汹汹地移动的人群，然后派生出「蜂拥而入」的动词，最后扩展到铺天盖地的昆虫或事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole camp on the march, people and animals moving as one dark mass.
core.cn: 核心意象：整座营地在行进，人与牲畜汇成一团移动的深色巨影。

branches.en: A large moving crowd keeps the mass image of the camp.
branches.cn: 「大群移动的人」保留了营地式的团块意象。

branches.en: The nomadic people on the move is the oldest historical sense.
branches.cn: 「流动的游牧部族」是历史上最早的义项。

branches.en: The verb for swarming in turns the crowd into an action.
branches.cn: 「蜂拥而入」的动词把人群变成了一个动作。

branches.en: Insects arriving in overwhelming numbers extend the same image beyond people.
branches.cn: 铺天盖地的昆虫把同样的意象从人扩展到动物。

branches.en: Both a crowd and a store of emails can become an unmanageable mass.
branches.cn: 人群和一大堆邮件都会变成难以应付的庞大数量。

intro.en: Horde is a loanword rather than a Latin compound, so its family is small: the plural, a British verb use, and a loose compound such as horde-like.
intro.cn: horde 是借词，不是拉丁语复合词，所以词族很小：复数形式、英式动词用法以及 horde-like 这类松散的组合。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no native word for horde; medieval Latin horda was itself borrowed from Polish and Mongol-Tatar usage, so the Latin links here are routes of borrowing rather than roots.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语本身没有表示 horde 的本族词；中古拉丁语 horda 是从波兰语与蒙古鞑靼用法借来的，所以这里的拉丁条目是借入路径，而不是词根。

items.meaning: a camp, army, or ruler's headquarters
items.example: Ordu is the earliest known form of the word.
items.exampleCN: ordu 是已知最早的词形。

items.example: Russian orda names the camps of steppe armies.
items.exampleCN: 俄语 orda 指草原军队的营地。

items.example: Polish horda passed the word into western Europe.
items.exampleCN: 波兰语 horda 把这个词传到了西欧。

items.example: Horde keeps the old camp meaning underneath.
items.exampleCN: horde 底下仍保留着古老的「营地」含义。

items.meaningCN: 许多这样的群体；成群的……
items.example: Hordes of fans is a very common pattern.
items.exampleCN: hordes of fans 是极常见的搭配。

items.example: British writers horde into the hall.
items.exampleCN: 英式写作者会用 horde in 表示涌进大厅。

items.example: The suffix -like makes horde-like.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -like 构成 horde-like 这个组合。

items.example: Hoard is spelled like horde but means a store.
items.exampleCN: hoard 拼写与 horde 相近，但意思是「储藏的财物」。

definition_zh: 使恐惧；使震惊；使反感
definition_en: to cause someone to feel great fear, shock, or strong disapproval
core_image: 看见可怕之物的一瞬间，汗毛竖起、浑身一抖，忍不住向后退
scene: 看到实验台上还在抽动的样本，学生们脸色发白，一步也不敢上前。The sight of the quivering specimen on the bench horrified the students.
sceneCN: 这里 horrify 是「使恐惧、使震惊」（第 1 个义项：令人产生强烈的恐惧与震惊）；句意：看到实验台上还在抽动的样本，学生们脸色发白，一步也不敢上前。

derivatives.zh: horrify 加 -ed 构成的过去分词形容词，义为「受到惊吓的；极度震惊的」
horrify 加 -ing 构成的现在分词形容词，义为「令人恐惧的；骇人的」
与 horrify 同源于拉丁语 horrere（毛发竖起），义为「恐怖；恐惧」
horror 加 -ific（造成……的）构成，义为「可怕的；骇人听闻的」

senses.title: To fill someone with fear
senses.definition: to make someone feel very frightened, as if seeing something dreadful
senses.definitionCN: 让人像看到可怕之物一样感到极度恐惧
senses.example: The dark shape horrifies the little boy.
senses.exampleCN: 那个黑影让小男孩十分害怕。
senses.why: Horrify is horror turned into a verb, and horror comes from a Latin word for the hair standing up in fear, so the verb means to put that shudder into someone.
senses.whyCN: horrify 是把名词 horror 动词化的结果，而 horror 源于拉丁语中表示「吓得毛发竖起」的词，所以动词就是「把这种战栗加诸某人」；核心画面是后背一凉、汗毛倒竖。

senses.title: To shock with bad news or an event
senses.definition: to cause someone to feel deeply shocked or upset at something unexpected and bad
senses.definitionCN: 让某人对意外的坏事感到极为震惊、难以接受
senses.example: The news of the crash horrified the whole town.
senses.exampleCN: 撞车事故的消息震惊了整个小镇。
senses.why: When the shuddering fear is caused by news or events rather than by a visible monster, the verb shades into a strong sense of shock.
senses.whyCN: 当引发战栗的不是眼前的怪物，而是消息或事件时，那种「毛骨悚然」就淡化成一种强烈的震惊。

senses.title: To drive someone to strong disapproval
senses.definition: to make someone feel strong moral disapproval or outrage
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生强烈的道德反感或愤慨
senses.example: Wasteful spending horrifies the voters.
senses.exampleCN: 挥霍开支让选民十分反感。
senses.why: Fear of something wretched easily hardens into moral disgust, so horrify can also mean to offend someone deeply.
senses.whyCN: 对糟糕之事的畏惧很容易硬化成道德上的厌恶，因此 horrify 也能表示「深深地冒犯、引起反感」。

senses.title: To make a feeling visible on the face
senses.definition: to show a frozen or appalled expression, as in the phrase a horrified look
senses.definitionCN: 流露出僵住或惊愕的表情，如 a horrified look 这类表达
senses.example: She gave her brother a horrified look.
senses.exampleCN: 她给了弟弟一个惊恐的眼神。
senses.why: The past participle horrified works as an adjective, so the internal shudder can become something you can see on a face.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词 horrified 可以当形容词用，于是内在的战栗变成能被人看见的神情：脸上凝固的那一瞬。

senses.title: To describe something repulsive
senses.definition: to describe a thing or situation as dreadful enough to revolt people, as in a horrifying accident
senses.definitionCN: 把某事或某种情形形容成可怕到令人厌恶的，如 a horrifying accident
senses.example: It was a horrifying accident that nobody expected.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一场谁也没料到的骇人事故。
senses.why: The present participle horrifying turns the action back on the cause, naming something that produces the dread.
senses.whyCN: 现在分词 horrifying 把动作反转到原因上，用来命名「会制造恐惧的那件事物」。

intro.en: Horrify is a verb built on horror, which comes from Latin horrere, to bristle or shudder; the verb itself is a later English formation and its first dates are approximate.
intro.cn: horrify 是在 horror 基础上构成的动词，而 horror 来自拉丁语 horrere（毛发竖起、战栗）；动词本身是英语后期自造，最早出现年代为约数。

items.en: A reconstructed root is given the sense to bristle; the link to the Latin family is generally accepted but not certain in every detail.
items.cn: 原始印欧语的重构词根被赋予「毛发竖起」之义；它与拉丁语词族的联系一般被接受，但细节并非全部确定。

items.en: Horrere meant to bristle, tremble or shudder, and Latin horror named a shuddering dread.
items.cn: horrere 意为毛发竖起、发抖、战栗；拉丁语 horror 指令人战栗的恐惧。

items.en: Old French took the noun as horrour or orror, meaning fear and a bristling of the hair.
items.cn: 古法语把该名词作 horrour / orror，意为恐惧与毛发竖起。

items.en: English borrowed the noun as horror in the fourteenth century, and later formed the adjective horrific and the verb horrify from it.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入名词 horror，后来又由它构成形容词 horrific 与动词 horrify。

items.en: Horrify spread from sheer fear to the shock of bad news and then to moral disapproval, while horrified became a common adjective.
items.cn: horrify 从纯粹的恐惧扩展到对坏消息的震惊，再扩展到道德上的反感；同时 horrified 成为常用形容词。

note.en: Horrify belongs to a family built on horror, and is close in meaning to frighten, terrify and appal.
note.cn: horrify 属于以 horror 为核心的词族，意义上与 frighten、terrify、appal 相近。

entries.definition: a feeling of great fear and shock
entries.definitionCN: 恐怖；恐惧

entries.definition: extremely frightening or shocking
entries.definitionCN: 可怕的；骇人听闻的

entries.definition: hateful and morally repulsive
entries.definitionCN: 可憎的；令人厌恶的

entries.definition: to frighten someone very much
entries.definitionCN: 使恐惧；使惊吓

entries.definition: to shock someone deeply, especially in a moral way
entries.definitionCN: 使惊骇；使骇然（尤指道德上的）

entries.definition: to make someone feel strong dislike
entries.definitionCN: 使厌恶；使作呕

normalIntro.en: Horrify is horror plus -ify, the suffix that turns a noun into a verb of making, so the word means to make someone full of horror.
normalIntro.cn: horrify 就是 horror 加 -ify（使……化）的动词后缀，字面意思是「使人充满 horror」。

normal.en: The family runs horror, horrify, horrific and abhorrent from one Latin root.
normal.cn: horror、horrify、horrific、abhorrent 来自同一个拉丁词根。

normal.en: Be horrified by is the usual pattern for reacting to something terrible.
normal.cn: be horrified by 是表示被某事吓到的常用结构。

normal.en: Horrifying describes the thing, horrified describes the person.
normal.cn: horrifying 形容事物，horrified 形容人。

normal.en: She was horrified to learn that the money was gone.
normal.cn: 她得知钱没了，十分震惊。

normal.en: Compare scare: scare is milder and more casual, while horrify means deep shock.
normal.cn: 对比 scare：scare 更轻更口语，horrify 指深深的惊恐与震惊。

abstract.en: Picture the hair on your arms lifting as a cold hand brushes your neck.
abstract.cn: 想象一只冰冷的手掠过脖颈，手臂上的汗毛齐齐竖起来。

abstract.en: See a letter being read aloud, and every face in the room going pale at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信被当众读出，屋里所有脸同时变白。

abstract.en: Feel the recoil when someone wastes food in front of a hungry family.
abstract.cn: 体会在饥寒人家面前浪费食物时，心里那种本能地缩回去的感觉。

examples.en: The reporter was horrified by the condition of the shelter.
examples.cn: 记者被收容所的状况震住了。

examples.en: Nothing horrified her more than the idea of waste.
examples.cn: 没有什么比浪费这个念头更让她反感。

examples.en: The horrified parents rushed to the gate.
examples.cn: 惊恐万分的父母冲向大门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「豁然发黑」——一到恐怖场面就眼前发黑、腿软发抖；这只是谐音联想，与拉丁语 horrere 的词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 horrere（毛发竖起、战栗），其名词 horror（战栗的恐惧）；英语先借入 horror，再加 -ify（使……化）构成 horrify，核心义「把人吓得汗毛倒竖」。更早的印欧语词根为重构形式，细节存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Horrify begins with raw fear, widens to the shock of bad news, hardens into moral outrage, and then splits into two adjectives for the face of the person and for the dreadful thing itself.
sensesIntro.cn: horrify 先表示纯粹的恐惧，再扩展到对坏消息的震惊，随后硬化成道德上的愤慨，最后分成两个形容词：一个写人的神情，一个写可怕的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shudder that starts at the neck and makes the hair stand up.
core.cn: 核心意象：从后颈开始的一阵战栗，让汗毛全部倒竖。

branches.en: Filling someone with fear is the core, bodily sense.
branches.cn: 让人充满恐惧是核心的身体感受义项。

branches.en: Shock at bad news turns visible fear into mental disturbance.
branches.cn: 对坏消息的震惊把可见的恐惧转成心理上的震荡。

branches.en: Moral outrage is fear hardened into disapproval.
branches.cn: 道德愤慨是由恐惧硬化而成的反感。

branches.en: The two participles split the action: one face, one cause.
branches.cn: 两个分词把动作一分为二：一个写神情，一个写起因。

branches.en: All three senses keep the same inner recoil from something dreadful.
branches.cn: 三个义项都保留着面对可怕之物时内心后退的那一下。

intro.en: Horrify is a transparent compound in English: the horror base plus the verb-forming suffix -ify, with its participles horrified and horrifying derived in turn.
intro.cn: horrify 在英语中结构清晰：horror 词基加上动词化后缀 -ify，再由此派生分词 horrified 与 horrifying。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is horrere, to bristle or shudder, with its noun horror; the -ify ending goes back to the Latin verb-forming -ificare as it passed through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源是 horrere（毛发竖起、战栗）及其名词 horror；-ify 词尾则可追溯到经法语传入的拉丁动词后缀 -ificare。

items.example: Horrere supplies the bodily shudder.
items.exampleCN: horrere 提供身体战栗的画面。

items.example: Horror is the noun behind the verb.
items.exampleCN: horror 是这个动词背后的名词。

items.meaning: to make or cause to be
items.example: The suffix -ify turns horror into horrify.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ify 把 horror 变成 horrify。

items.example: Horrifying describes a scene that causes dread.
items.exampleCN: horrifying 描述引起恐惧的场景。

items.example: Horrified describes the person who feels it.
items.exampleCN: horrified 描述感受到恐惧的人。

items.example: The suffix -ific forms horrific.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ific 构成 horrific。

items.example: The prefix ab- forms abhorrent from horror.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ab- 由 horrere 构成 abhorrent。

items.example: The suffix -ent finishes abhorrent.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ent 收尾构成 abhorrent。

items.example: Abhorrent shares the shuddering root.
items.exampleCN: abhorrent 共享「战栗」词根。

definition_zh: 虻；马蝇（叮咬牲畜、吸取血液的大型蝇类）
definition_en: a large stout fly that bites horses and other animals and feeds on their blood
core_image: 一头大个头的灰黑色蝇虫伏在马的肚腹上，翅膀平张，口器深深扎进马皮
scene: 牧场上，马儿不停甩动尾巴、暴躁地踢腿，想把叮在肚皮上的大蝇驱走。In the meadow the horse twitched its tail to drive off a single horsefly.
sceneCN: 这里 horsefly 是「虻、马蝇」（第 1 个义项：叮咬牲畜、靠吸血为生的大型蝇类）；句意：牧场上，马儿不停甩动尾巴、暴躁地踢腿，想把叮在肚皮上的大蝇驱走。

forms.label: 复数（较少见，复合词不变形）

derivatives.zh: 由 -y 变 -ies 构成的常规复数，义为「多只虻」
复合词的第一部分，义为「马」；民间常把叮咬马匹的虫冠以 horse
复合词的第二部分，义为「蝇」；horse + fly 直接点明这是与马有关的蝇
horse（马）+ botfly（胃蝇）构成的近邻复合词，指在马胃里寄生的胃蝇

senses.title: A large biting fly of horses
senses.definition: a large fly with a strong, thick body that bites horses and cattle to feed on blood
senses.definitionCN: 体型大、身体粗壮，靠叮咬马和牛吸取血液的蝇类
senses.example: A horsefly settled on the old mare and bit her neck.
senses.exampleCN: 一只虻落在老母马上，咬了它的脖子。
senses.why: The compound simply names the fly that horses suffer from, and the same animal carries the Latin name tabanus.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是复合词，字面即「叮马的蝇」，命名方式是把受害的牲畜直接放进名字里；同一种昆虫在拉丁语中叫 tabanus。

senses.title: Its painful bite
senses.definition: the sharp, painful bite that such a fly gives, and the red mark it leaves
senses.definitionCN: 这种蝇造成的锐痛叮咬，以及留下的红肿痕迹
senses.example: The horsefly bite left a red lump on his arm.
senses.exampleCN: 虻叮过的地方在他胳膊上留下一个红肿的包。
senses.why: Because the fly cuts the skin and drinks blood, the word is often used for the bite itself, especially in British English.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种蝇会切开口子吸血，所以 horsefly 也常用作虻咬这个词，英式英语中尤其普遍；核心画面仍是「扎进去、留下红印」。

senses.title: A pest of horses and cattle
senses.definition: the insect seen as an agricultural pest that troubles livestock throughout the summer
senses.definitionCN: 把这种昆虫视为整个夏天都能骚扰牲畜的农业害虫
senses.example: Farmers cover the shed doors to keep the horseflies away.
senses.exampleCN: 农场主把棚门遮起来，不让虻靠近。
senses.why: Once the fly is known to be a livestock pest, the word can stand for the nuisance as a class in farming talk.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这种蝇被认定为牲畜害虫，这个词在农事话语中就可以作为一个类别，代指那类恼人的骚扰。

senses.title: A nuisance that plagues vehicles and walkers
senses.definition: a persistent, annoying thing or person that harasses others like these flies do
senses.definitionCN: 像这种蝇一样纠缠不休、令人烦躁的事物或人
senses.example: A horsefly of a salesman kept circling the table.
senses.exampleCN: 一个像马蝇一样缠人的推销员一直在桌边转。
senses.why: The buzz and the sting make a convenient image for any annoyance that returns again and again.
senses.whyCN: 嗡嗡声加上一刺，为任何反复回来的烦恼提供了现成的意象：赶走了又回来。

senses.title: The family tabanidae
senses.definition: in scientific use, any member of the fly family that contains horseflies and deerflies
senses.definitionCN: 在科学用法中，指虻科中包括马蝇和鹿虻在内的任何成员
senses.example: The museum list every horsefly found in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把当地发现的每一种虻都列了出来。
senses.why: Insect science groups the biting horseflies under a family name, and that name is Latin, so the everyday word and the Latin name meet here.
senses.whyCN: 昆虫学会把这类叮咬性的虻归在一个科名下，而那个科名正是拉丁语，日常词与拉丁学名在这里碰头。

intro.en: Horsefly is an English compound, horse plus fly, first recorded in the sixteenth century. English once used the Latin loan stimulus for this insect, with a diminutive asilus, and those forms still stand in insect names today.
intro.cn: horsefly 是英语复合词 horse + fly，始于 16 世纪。英语早期曾用拉丁借词 stimulus 指这种昆虫，另有指小形式 asilus，这些词形至今仍见于昆虫学名。

items.en: The first element is the ordinary horse word, whose deeper root refers to running; it is not a Latin word.
items.cn: 第一部分为普通的名词 horse，其更早词根与「奔跑」有关，并非拉丁词。

items.en: The insect was named in Latin stimulus, a goad or stinging spur, with a diminutive asilus for the smaller kinds.
items.cn: 这种昆虫在拉丁语中叫 stimulus（刺棒、带刺的马刺），较小的种类则用指小形式 asilus。

items.en: The compound horsefly is first recorded in the sixteenth century; early spellings vary, but the two parts are always horse and fly.
items.cn: 复合词 horsefly 最早见于 16 世纪；早期拼写不一，但两部分始终是 horse 与 fly。

items.en: The old Latin stimulus fell out of every speech, surviving as a technical term, while horsefly spread as the plain everyday name.
items.cn: 古老的拉丁词 stimulus 退出日常口语，只留作术语，而 horsefly 作为通俗名称传播开来。

items.en: Modern dictionaries write the compound as horsefly, while horse fly still appears, and insect science keeps the family name based on tabanus.
items.cn: 现代词典把它写作 horsefly，horse fly 仍可见；昆虫学则以 tabanus 为基础保留科名。

note.en: Horsefly is a compound ending in fly, so it keeps company with other horse-derived compounds and with fly words of similar shape.
note.cn: horsefly 是以 fly 结尾的复合词，因此它与以 horse 构成的其他复合词相邻，也与形似的 fly 类词相邻。

entries.definition: the hair taken from a horse
entries.definitionCN: 马毛

entries.definition: a unit for measuring the power of an engine
entries.definitionCN: 马力（功率单位）

entries.definition: a root vegetable with a very hot, sharp taste
entries.definitionCN: 辣根。与看似的「马萝卜」无关，horse- 在此并非指马

entries.definition: a fly whose young develop inside animals
entries.definitionCN: 胃蝇；狂蝇

entries.definition: a smaller relative of the horsefly that also bites
entries.definitionCN: 鹿虻（虻科中较小的叮咬蝇类）

entries.definition: a common domestic fly that does not bite
entries.definitionCN: 家蝇（不叮咬的常见蝇）

normalIntro.en: Horsefly is built like a label: the animal it bites plus the word for fly, so the name itself tells you where to look.
normalIntro.cn: horsefly 像一个标签：被叮的牲畜加「蝇」，名字本身就告诉你该去哪儿找它。

normal.en: The plural changes y to ies: horseflies.
normal.cn: 复数把词尾 y 变成 ies：horseflies。

normal.en: Latin stimulus once meant this very insect, so the modern word has a surprising learned cousin.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 stimulus 曾经就指这种昆虫，所以现代词藏着一个出人意料的学术亲戚。

normal.en: Horseflies bite horses, cattle and stubborn walkers alike.
normal.cn: 虻会叮马、叮牛，也会叮不肯走的行路人。

normal.en: A horsefly bite is usually a painful red lump.
normal.cn: 被虻叮了通常是一个又痛又红的包。

normal.en: Compare housefly: houseflies live in houses, horseflies live around livestock.
normal.cn: 对比 housefly：家蝇住在宅子里，horsefly 则围着牲畜转。

abstract.en: Picture a big grey fly landing on the flank of a horse, and the horse stamping in fury.
abstract.cn: 想象一只灰黑色大蝇落在马的肋腹上，马气得直跺蹄。

abstract.en: See a red mark in the shape of a fly left on a forearm.
abstract.cn: 想象小臂上留下的一个蝇形红印。

abstract.en: Think of a swarm of dark dots over a cattle herd on a hot afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象炎热的午后，牛群头顶盘着一团黑点。

examples.en: The horseflies were so bad that the herd stayed in the shade all afternoon.
examples.cn: 虻实在太多，牛群整个下午都躲在阴凉里。

examples.en: Riders carry a small net to keep the horseflies away from their mounts.
examples.cn: 骑手会带一张小网，把虻挡在马外。

examples.en: A field study traced each horsefly back to the pond it hatched in.
examples.cn: 一项野外研究把每只虻都追溯到了它孵出的那天水塘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「霍斯弗莱」——想象一位叫霍斯的人被大蝇追着满场跑；这只是谐音联想，与 horse 加 fly 的构词无关。

root: 英语复合词 horse（马）+ fly（蝇），16 世纪起见于文献；更早英语曾借拉丁语 stimulus（刺棒）指这种虫，另有指小形式 asilus。horse 与 fly 均非拉丁来源。

sensesIntro.en: Horsefly names the insect itself, then its painful bite, then the pest of farm life, then any nagging nuisance, and finally a whole branch of insect science.
sensesIntro.cn: horsefly 先给这只昆虫命名，再指它的叮咬，然后指牧场害虫，又引申为惹人厌的纠缠者，最后进入昆虫学的分类体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stout grey fly digging into the flank of a horse.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只粗壮的灰黑色蝇把口器扎进马的肋腹。

branches.en: The insect itself is the plain naming sense.
branches.cn: 昆虫本身是最基本的命名义项。

branches.en: The bite is the action felt on the skin.
branches.cn: 叮咬是落在皮肤上的那个动作。

branches.en: The farm pest is the insect seen by cattle owners.
branches.cn: 牧场害虫是牧户眼中的那只蝇。

branches.en: The nuisance sense borrows the fly as an image of nagging.
branches.cn: 「惹人厌者」义项借这种蝇来比喻纠缠不休。

branches.en: The everyday name and the scientific family name describe the same insects.
branches.cn: 日常名与科学科名指的是同一批昆虫。

intro.en: Horsefly is an English compound with no prefix or suffix of its own; the plural, the split spelling and the horse compounds around it show how the two halves work.
intro.cn: horsefly 是英语复合词，本身没有前后缀；复数、分写形式以及周边以 horse 构成的复合词，展示了这两个成分如何拼合。

latinIntro.en: Only the old Latin name of the insect is Latin here; the two halves of the compound come from ordinary English, so these Latin entries are borrowed names rather than roots of the word.
latinIntro.cn: 这里唯一带拉丁语成分的是这种昆虫的旧名；复合词的两半都来自普通英语，所以这些拉丁条目只是借来的名称，不是单词的词根。

items.meaning: a large animal that people ride
items.example: Horse names the animal the fly bites.
items.exampleCN: horse 点名了被叮的动物。

items.meaning: a small insect with two wings
items.example: Fly names the insect type.
items.exampleCN: fly 点名了昆虫的类型。

items.meaning: change for a singular ending in y
items.meaningCN: 词尾为 y 的单数变复数规则
items.example: Horseflies follows this rule.
items.exampleCN: horseflies 遵循这条规则。

items.meaning: the same insect, written as two words
items.example: Horse fly is an accepted variant spelling.
items.exampleCN: horse fly 是可接受的分写形式。

items.meaning: a fly whose young live in animals
items.example: Botfly shows the same fly building pattern.
items.exampleCN: botfly 展示了同样的「某物 + fly」构词模式。

items.meaning: a small biting relative of the horsefly
items.example: Deerfly keeps the animal plus fly pattern.
items.exampleCN: deerfly 保留了「动物 + fly」的模式。

items.example: Housefly pairs a place with fly.
items.exampleCN: housefly 把地点与 fly 配在一起。

items.meaning: the old Latin name of this insect
items.example: Stimulus once meant the horsefly in English.
items.exampleCN: stimulus 在英语中曾指 horsefly。

items.example: Asilus is the diminutive insect name.
items.exampleCN: asilus 是指小形式。

items.meaning: the generic name of biting horseflies
items.example: Tabanus is the genus name today.

latinEntries.meaning: a horsefly, often a smaller one

definition_zh: 园艺；园艺学；园艺栽培
definition_en: the art or science of growing fruit, vegetables, flowers and ornamental plants, usually in a garden
core_image: 一方围起来的园子：弯腰的人用锄头和剪刀侍弄每一株植物
scene: 周末早晨，一位老人戴着手套在自家园子里给玫瑰剪枝。Every weekend, the old man spends hours on horticulture in his small back garden.
sceneCN: 这里 horticulture 是「园艺」（第 1 个义项：种植花果蔬菜的技艺）；句意：每到周末，这位老人都会花好几个小时在小后院做园艺。

derivatives.zh: horticulture 去 e 加形容词后缀 -al 而成，义为「园艺的」
horticulture 加表示「人」的后缀 -ist 而成，义为「园艺家」
horticultural 加 -ist 而成，与 horticulturist 同义，指「园艺师」
horticultural 加副词后缀 -ly 而成，义为「就园艺而言」

senses.title: The art of garden cultivation
senses.definition: the skill of growing flowers, fruit and vegetables, especially in a garden
senses.definitionCN: 在园子里种植花木、果树和蔬菜的技艺
senses.example: Her horticulture skills keep the whole terrace in bloom.
senses.exampleCN: 她的园艺本领让整条街的露台常年开花。
senses.why: The Latin hortus means garden, so the word starts as the very craft practised inside a walled garden.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 hortus 意为「园子」，所以这个词最初就是指在围起来的园子里干的活计。

senses.title: The science of plant growing
senses.definition: the scientific study of growing and caring for cultivated plants
senses.definitionCN: 研究栽培植物的生长与养护的科学
senses.example: Horticulture is offered as a subject at agricultural colleges.
senses.exampleCN: 农学院里设有园艺学这门学科。
senses.why: The second half from Latin cultura means cultivating, so the craft became a systematic science when its methods were studied.
senses.whyCN: 后缀部分来自拉丁语 cultura（耕作），当种植方法被系统研究时，这项手艺就变成了一门科学。

senses.title: Commercial plant growing
senses.definition: the large-scale industry of raising plants for sale, such as nurseries and cut flowers
senses.definitionCN: 育苗场、切花等以出售植物为目的的大规模产业
senses.example: Horticulture now supplies most of the cut flowers in city shops.
senses.exampleCN: 如今城里的花店大多由园艺产业供应切花。
senses.why: The garden image widens from one household to large glasshouses, but the action of tending plants stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 画面从一家一户的园子扩展到大型温室，但「侍弄植物」这个动作始终没变。

senses.title: Gardening as a practical activity
senses.definition: the hands-on work of planning, planting and pruning in a garden
senses.definitionCN: 在园中规划、栽种、修剪的实际劳作
senses.example: He took up horticulture as a hobby after retiring.
senses.exampleCN: 他退休后把园艺当作爱好。
senses.why: Because the word names the activity itself, it can also be used for the everyday pastime of tending plants.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本身指的是这项活动，因此也可以用来指日常种花养草的消遣。

senses.title: The trade and business of gardens
senses.definition: the profession and market built around garden design, maintenance and plant supply
senses.definitionCN: 围绕花园设计、养护与苗木供应形成的职业与市场
senses.example: Many new jobs have opened up in horticulture and garden design.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺与花园设计领域出现了许多新工作。
senses.why: Once the craft serves paying customers, the walled garden turns into an industry with firms and careers.
senses.whyCN: 当这门手艺开始服务付费客户，围起来的园子就变成了有公司和职业的行业。

intro.en: Horticulture was formed in seventeenth-century English from Latin hortus, garden, and cultura, cultivation.
intro.cn: horticulture 在十七世纪英语中由拉丁语 hortus（园子）与 cultura（耕作）组合而成，外来构词特征明显。

items.en: Hortus means a garden or enclosed plot of ground.
items.cn: hortus 意为园子、圈起来的一块地。

items.en: Cultura comes from colere, to till, and means cultivation.
items.cn: cultura 来自 colere（耕作），意为栽培、耕作。

items.en: Horticulture is coined by joining hortus and cultura, probably after agriculture.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语把 hortus 与 cultura 拼合，可能仿照 agriculture 的构词方式造出 horticulture。

items.en: The word spreads with the fashion for walled kitchen gardens and glasshouses.
items.cn: 随着围墙菜园和温室的风行，这个词逐渐普及。

items.en: Horticulture grows into an academic subject and a commercial industry.
items.cn: 现代英语中，horticulture 发展成一门学科和一个商业行业。

note.en: Horticulture belongs to the garden family, close to agriculture, agronomy, gardening and botany.
note.cn: horticulture 属于「园子」一族，与 agriculture、agronomy、gardening、botany 相邻。

entries.definition: relating to the growing of garden plants
entries.definitionCN: 园艺的

entries.definition: a person who is skilled in horticulture
entries.definitionCN: 园艺家；园艺师

entries.definition: the science and practice of farming land
entries.definitionCN: 农业；农学；与园艺同用表示「耕作」的词尾，只是前半部分指田野

entries.definition: the activity of tending a garden
entries.definitionCN: 园艺；种花种菜（更口语，多指业余爱好）

entries.definition: the scientific study of plants
entries.definitionCN: 植物学（偏纯科学，不涉及栽种实操）

entries.definition: the science of growing crops and managing farmland
entries.definitionCN: 农学；农艺学（面向大田作物）

normalIntro.en: Horticulture is two Latin blocks: hortus, a garden, plus cultura, cultivation.
normalIntro.cn: horticulture 是两块拉丁积木：hortus（园子）加 cultura（耕作）。

normal.en: Hortus means garden, and it returns in compounds such as horticulture.
normal.cn: hortus 意为园子，它在 horticulture 这类合成词中复活。

normal.en: The same word comes from treating plants in a garden rather than a field.
normal.cn: 这个词正是从照料园里的植物而非田里的作物而来的。

normal.en: The ending looks like the one in agriculture, and both words end in cultivation.
normal.cn: 词尾与 agriculture 相似，两词都以「耕作」收尾。

normal.en: A person who does it is a horticulturist, simply the noun plus -ist.
normal.cn: 做园艺的人叫 horticulturist，就是名词加表示人的后缀 -ist。

normal.en: The adjective is horticultural, so the -al ending marks the adjective.
normal.cn: 形容词是 horticultural，后缀 -al 标记形容词词性。

abstract.en: Picture a walled garden with a gardener bending over a rose bush.
abstract.cn: 想象一座围墙花园，园丁正俯身修剪玫瑰。

abstract.en: See a glasshouse full of seedlings, each in its own pot.
abstract.cn: 想象一座温室，里面每株幼苗各占一个小盆。

abstract.en: Imagine a flower shop whose blooms all came from one nursery.
abstract.cn: 想象一家花店，所有鲜花都来自同一个苗圃。

examples.en: She studied horticulture before opening her own nursery.
examples.cn: 她在开办自己的苗圃之前学过园艺。

examples.en: Horticulture and agriculture both deal with plants, but on different scales.
examples.cn: 园艺与农业都与植物打交道，只是规模不同。

examples.en: The hospital runs a small horticultural project for recovering patients.
examples.cn: 这家医院为康复中的病人开展了一个小型园艺项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「花体+靠倒」——花草被摆出漂亮的花体，园丁靠它把庭院「靠」得整齐；这只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 hortus（园子）加 cultura（耕作、栽培），十七世纪英语仿照 agriculture 组合成 horticulture，核心义「在园子里耕作」。

sensesIntro.en: Horticulture moves from the craft inside a garden to a science, an industry, a hands-on hobby and a trade.
sensesIntro.cn: horticulture 从园子里的手艺出发，发展为学科、产业、劳作与行业几个方向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walled garden where a gardener bends over a bush.
core.cn: 核心意象：围墙花园里，园丁俯身侍弄一丛植物。

branches.en: The hands-on craft and the pastime both come straight from the garden image.
branches.cn: 动手的技艺与日常消遣都直接来自园子这一画面。

branches.en: The science branch specialises the same cultivation into formal study.
branches.cn: 学科分支把同一种栽培提升为正式研究。

branches.en: The commercial branch moves the garden to nurseries and glasshouses.
branches.cn: 商业分支把园子搬到苗圃和温室。

branches.en: The trade branch turns the craft into jobs, firms and markets.
branches.cn: 行业分支把手艺变成工作岗位、公司与市场。

branches.en: Selling plants and building a horticulture business go together.
branches.cn: 出售植物与开创园艺生意是同一件事的两面。

intro.en: Horticulture is a modern compound of two Latin elements, with horticultural and horticulturist built on it.
intro.cn: horticulture 是两个拉丁成分组成的现代合成词，英语围绕它构成 horticultural 与 horticulturist。

latinIntro.en: Latin hortus means garden, and cultura, from colere, means cultivation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 hortus 意为园子，cultura 来自 colere，意为耕作、栽培。

items.example: The root hort- appears in horticulture.
items.exampleCN: 词根 hort- 出现在 horticulture 中。

items.example: Hortus is the first half of the word.
items.exampleCN: hortus 是这个单词的前半部分。

items.example: The ending -culture marks the act of cultivating.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -culture 标记栽培这一行为。

items.example: Cultura comes from the verb colere.
items.exampleCN: cultura 来自动词 colere。

items.example: Agriculture is the likely model for this compound.
items.exampleCN: agriculture 很可能就是它的构词样板。

items.example: Gardening is the plainer everyday word.
items.exampleCN: gardening 是更朴素的日常说法。

items.example: The suffix -al forms horticultural.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 horticultural。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms horticulturist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 horticulturist。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms horticulturally.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 horticulturally。

definition_zh: 软管；水龙带；用软管冲洗；长筒袜
definition_en: a long flexible tube used to carry water, or to wash something with such a tube
core_image: 花园里一圈盘起的水管：拧开龙头，水便顺着管子喷出去
scene: 园丁把水龙头接到胶皮管上，给新栽的树苗浇水。The gardener attached the hose to the tap and watered the young trees.
sceneCN: 这里 hose 是「软管」（第 1 个义项：输水的软管）；句意：园丁把软管接到水龙头上，给新栽的小树浇水。

derivatives.zh: hose 与 pipe 合成，特指园艺浇水的胶皮水管，多见于英式英语
hose（长筒袜）加集合名词后缀 -iery 而成，义为「针织袜类」
hose 加表示职业的后缀 -ier 而成，旧指「袜商」
hose 加 -ing 构成的动名词，义为「用软管冲洗」

senses.title: A flexible tube for liquid
senses.definition: a long tube made of rubber or plastic that carries water or another liquid
senses.definitionCN: 用橡胶或塑料制成的、输送水或其他液体的长管
senses.example: Water sprayed out of a split in the hose.
senses.exampleCN: 水从软管的裂口处喷了出来。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a hollow stocking-like tube, and a water pipe is simply that hollow shape turned into plumbing.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意思是中空的袜筒状管子，而水管不过把这个中空形状变成了输水的管道。

senses.title: To wash something with a hose
senses.definition: to clean or wet something by directing water through a hose
senses.definitionCN: 通过软管引水来清洗或浇湿某物
senses.example: They hosed the muddy car before driving out.
senses.exampleCN: 他们开车出门前用软管把满是泥的车冲洗干净。
senses.why: Once the tube exists, using it becomes a verb: the object of the noun turns into the action of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 管子一旦存在，用它就成了动词：名词所代表的东西转过身变成了动作。

senses.title: In firefighting, a pressure hose
senses.definition: a strong wide tube used by firefighters to direct water at high pressure
senses.definitionCN: 消防员用来高压喷水的粗而结实的水带
senses.example: Firefighters dragged a heavy hose up three flights of stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员拖着沉重的水带爬上三楼。
senses.why: The same hollow tube is made bigger and stronger when it must carry urgent, high-pressure water.
senses.whyCN: 同一种中空管子，在需要承受高压紧急送水时就被做得更大更结实。

senses.title: A stocking or long sock
senses.definition: a close-fitting garment covering the foot and lower leg, often knitted
senses.definitionCN: 包裹脚与小腿、多为针织的紧身衣物
senses.example: In the old market, merchants sold silk hose in bright colours.
senses.exampleCN: 在老集市上，商人们出售颜色鲜艳的丝质长筒袜。
senses.why: The clothing sense is the historical origin: a leg covering is also a soft hollow tube pulled over the leg.
senses.whyCN: 服装义是历史源头：包住腿的衣物同样是一根套在腿上的中空软管。

senses.title: To spray water over a wide area
senses.definition: to direct a steady flow of water over a lawn, path or garden
senses.definitionCN: 把水流持续浇洒在草坪、小路或花园上
senses.example: Nobody should hose the lawn in the middle of a drought.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱期间谁都不该用水管给草坪浇水。
senses.why: From washing one object, the verb widens to wetting an area, such as a lawn or a street.
senses.whyCN: 从洗刷一个物件，动词扩展到浇湿一整片区域，比如草坪或街道。

senses.title: Informal, to cheat or attack secretly
senses.definition: to cheat someone or criticise them, in informal slang use
senses.definitionCN: 在非正式俚语中，指欺骗某人或抨击某人
senses.example: He felt he had been hosed by the second-hand dealer.
senses.exampleCN: 他觉得自己被那个二手商骗了。
senses.why: Slang pictures a person being drenched by a hidden stream of water, so being targeted unfairly feels like being hosed.
senses.whyCN: 俚语把被突然泼一身水的感觉用于比喻，被不公平地针对就像是被人用水管浇了一通。

senses.title: Hosiery, the goods trade term
senses.definition: stockings, socks and tights sold together as a class of goods
senses.definitionCN: 作为一类商品一起出售的长袜、短袜与连裤袜
senses.example: The shop on the corner specialises in socks and other hosiery.
senses.exampleCN: 街角那家店专门卖袜子一类的针织品。
senses.why: Shops needed one word for all knitted legwear, so the old clothing noun grew into the collective trade term.
senses.whyCN: 商家需要一个词统称所有针织腿部衣物，于是旧的服装义长出了集合名词。

senses.title: To fit with a hose
senses.definition: to connect an appliance or pipe to a water supply with a hose
senses.definitionCN: 用软管把设备或管道接到水源上
senses.example: They hosed the washing machine to the cold tap.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把洗衣机接到冷水龙头上。
senses.why: The meaning narrows from washing to the fitting action, tying the noun back to its job of carrying water.
senses.whyCN: 含义从冲洗收窄到安装对接，把名词重新拉回「输水」这一本职。

intro.en: Hose goes back to Germanic words for a leg covering, a stocking made of a hollow tube.
intro.cn: hose 可追溯到日耳曼语中指腿部衣物的词，原指用中空筒形布料做成的长袜。

items.en: The word family covers stockings and leggings, probably from a root meaning covering.
items.cn: 这一词族指长袜与护腿，一般认为来自表示「覆盖」的词根。

items.en: Hose names a leg covering in early English.
items.cn: 在早期英语中，hose 指一种腿部衣物。

items.en: Hose becomes the usual word for stockings worn by both sexes.
items.cn: 中古英语中，hose 成为长袜的常用词。

items.en: Hose is applied to a flexible tube, on the image of a hollow stocking.
items.cn: 十六世纪前后，hose 借「中空袜筒」的形象被用于指柔性管子。

items.en: Garden and fire hoses make the tube sense dominant, and the verb hose appears.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，花园水管与消防水带使「管子」义成为主流，动词 hose 也随之出现。

note.en: Hose sits between tube vocabulary and clothing vocabulary, close to pipe, hosiery and garden words.
note.cn: hose 处在「管子」与「衣物」两片词场之间，近于 pipe、hosiery 以及园艺类词。

entries.definitionCN: 园艺浇水用的胶皮水管

entries.definition: stockings, socks and tights as goods
entries.definitionCN: 针织袜类商品

entries.definition: a tube for carrying water or gas, often rigid
entries.definitionCN: 管道，常指固定不弯的硬管

entries.definition: a long hollow cylinder
entries.definitionCN: 管；筒（最笼统的上位词）

entries.definition: a device that sprays water over an area
entries.definitionCN: 喷灌器；洒水装置

entries.definitionCN: 长筒袜（对应 hose 的旧义）

normalIntro.en: Hose is a hollow stocking first and a water pipe second, and the tube image is the easy one to keep.
normalIntro.cn: hose 先是中空的袜筒，后是中空的水管，记住「中空」这一形象即可。

normal.en: A garden hose is the everyday item, and it looks like a long soft stocking.
normal.cn: 花园水管是最常见的实物，它就像一只长长的软袜。

normal.en: The phrase hose down means to wash something with a copious flow.
normal.cn: 短语 hose down 意为用大量水流冲洗某物。

normal.en: Firefighters use a fire hose, so the same noun grows stronger for emergencies.
normal.cn: 消防员用的是 fire hose，同一个名词在紧急场景中变得更强韧。

normal.en: The oldest sense is stockings, and hosiery keeps that old meaning alive in shops.
normal.cn: 最古老的意思是长袜，hosiery 在商店里让这一旧义延续至今。

normal.en: Compare pipe, which is usually rigid, while a hose bends and coils.
normal.cn: 对比 pipe：后者通常是硬管，而 hose 可以弯曲盘绕。

abstract.en: Picture a green coil of hose looped around a tap.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈绿色水管盘绕在水龙头上。

abstract.en: Imagine water punching a hole in a worn black tube and spraying across a path.
abstract.cn: 想象水从磨损的黑管子上冲出一个洞，横着喷过小路。

abstract.en: Think of a firefighter steadying a thick canvas tube against the pressure.
abstract.cn: 想象消防员顶着水压稳住一根粗帆布水带。

examples.en: Could you pass me the hose so I can water the plants?
examples.cn: 能把水管递给我吗，我好浇浇花。

examples.en: He hosed the dust off the patio after the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨过后，他用水管把露台上的尘土冲掉。

examples.en: The hotel laundry uses a long hose to fill the tubs.
examples.cn: 酒店洗衣房用一根长软管给水池注水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「后水」——接在龙头后边出水的那条管子；也可以用「好湿」联想被水管浇湿。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 源自日耳曼语指腿部衣物的词（一般认为来自「覆盖」词根）→ 古英语 hose（长袜）→ 十六世纪借「中空袜筒」的形象指软管，核心义「中空软筒」。

sensesIntro.en: Hose begins as a stocking, becomes the soft hollow tube, then splits into a noun for tubes and clothes and a verb for washing.
sensesIntro.cn: hose 从长袜起步，经「中空软筒」演化为管子的名词，再分出衣物义与冲洗的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coiled hollow tube that pours water.
core.cn: 核心意象：盘成一圈的中空管子，正往外吐水。

branches.en: The garden tube and the fire hose are the same object at different strengths.
branches.cn: 花园水管与消防水带是同一物件在不同强度下的版本。

branches.en: The verb branch covers both washing an object and spraying an area.
branches.cn: 动词分支既包括冲洗物件，也包括浇洒一片区域。

branches.en: The stocking sense survives in clothing and in its collective trade term.
branches.cn: 长袜义在衣物本身与集合商贸词中延续。

branches.en: The slang branch borrows the feeling of being soaked by a hidden jet.
branches.cn: 俚语分支借用了被暗处水流浇透的感受。

branches.en: Having a hose and fitting a hose both come from the carrying-water function.
branches.cn: 拥有软管与接上软管都源自输水这一功能。

intro.en: Hose is a short Germanic word; the English around it is built with compounds and suffixes such as -iery and -ier.
intro.cn: hose 是简短的日耳曼语词，围绕它的英语词多用合成与 -iery、-ier 等后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Hose is not of Latin origin, so its Latin relatives are indirect borrowing rather than same-root words.
latinIntro.cn: hose 并非拉丁语来源，所谓拉丁同族实为间接借词，而非同一词根。

items.example: Hose is the base word of the whole pair.
items.exampleCN: hose 是这一对词的基础词。

items.example: The element -pipe forms hosepipe.
items.exampleCN: 成分 -pipe 构成 hosepipe。

items.example: Hosepipe names the tube explicitly by its function.
items.exampleCN: hosepipe 用功能把这种管子说清楚。

items.example: The suffix -ier forms hosier.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ier 构成 hosier。

items.example: The suffix -iery forms hosiery.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -iery 构成 hosiery。

items.example: Hosiery collects all knitted legwear.
items.exampleCN: hosiery 集合所有针织腿部衣物。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms hosing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 hosing。

items.example: The particle down forms the phrase hose down.
items.exampleCN: 小品词 down 构成短语 hose down。

definition_zh: 好客的；殷勤待客的；热情友好的；宜人的；易接受的
definition_en: friendly and generous to guests, and welcoming to strangers
core_image: 敞开的木门：主人站在门边，把过路的陌生人请进屋里先喝上一杯
scene: 村里人家在门前摆出长桌，招呼远道而来的客人坐下吃饭。The village families are famously hospitable to travellers who lose their way in the hills.
sceneCN: 这里 hospitable 是「好客的」（第 1 个义项：热情款待客人）；句意：这些村里人家以好客闻名，凡是山里迷了路的旅人都受到他们的款待。

pos.zh: 好客的；殷勤待客的；热情友好的；宜人的；易接受的

collocations.zh: 适宜的环境；友好的环境

derivatives.zh: hospitable 同源的拉丁名词 hospitalitas 进入英语后的形式，义为「好客；款待」
hospitable 去 e 加副词后缀 -ly 而成，义为「热情地；好客地」
与 hospitable 同源：拉丁语 hospitalia 原指接待客人的房舍，词义转向收治病人之处
hospitable 加否定前缀 in- 而成，义为「不好客的；条件恶劣的」

senses.title: Generous to guests
senses.definition: friendly and generous in welcoming and entertaining guests
senses.definitionCN: 在迎接和招待客人时热情大方的
senses.example: The family were so hospitable that we stayed two extra nights.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人太热情好客，我们多住了两晚。
senses.why: The Latin root hospes joins host and guest, so being hospitable is acting as a generous host rather than a closed door.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 hospes 同时含「主人」与「客人」，所以 hospitable 就是做个慷慨的主人，而不是关上大门。

senses.title: Friendly to strangers
senses.titleCN: 热情友好的；乐于接纳的
senses.definition: kind and open towards people one does not know
senses.definitionCN: 对不认识的人善良而敞开心扉
senses.example: People in the port were surprisingly hospitable towards visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 港口一带的人对来访者出奇地友好热情。
senses.why: Because hospes also means guest and stranger, the word extends from invited guests to any newcomer.
senses.whyCN: 因为 hospes 也可以指客人和外来者，所以词义从受邀的客人扩展到任何初来的人。

senses.title: Suitable for creating life
senses.definition: providing good conditions for people, animals or plants to live
senses.definitionCN: 为人和动植物提供良好生存条件的
senses.example: The valley is too cold and dry to be hospitable to crops.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷过于寒冷干燥，不适宜农作物生长。
senses.why: The open, welcoming image is transferred from a host to a place, so a good landscape is one that receives life warmly.
senses.whyCN: 敞开的接纳意象从主人转移到地方上，于是良好的自然环境就被说成是热情地接纳生命的。

senses.title: Searchable by a person or machine
senses.titleCN: 易被检索的；便于访问的
senses.definition: easy for a user or software tool to search or gather data from
senses.definitionCN: 方便用户或软件工具检索、收集数据的
senses.example: The archive is now open and hospitable to automated search.
senses.exampleCN: 这个档案库如今开放，并且便于自动化检索。
senses.why: Modern technology borrows the welcome image: a website that lets visitors in easily is hospitable to them.
senses.whyCN: 现代技术借用了那段欢迎的意象：一个让访客轻松进入的网站，就是对该访客好客的。

senses.title: Receptive to new ideas
senses.definition: willing to listen to new ideas, criticism or suggestions
senses.definitionCN: 愿意听取新想法、批评或建议的
senses.example: The editor was hospitable to fresh ideas from young writers.
senses.exampleCN: 这位编辑乐于接纳年轻作者的奇思妙想。
senses.why: The guest becomes an idea; welcoming it warmly is the same gesture as welcoming a visitor.
senses.whyCN: 客人变成了一个想法；热情地把它迎进门，与迎接客人的姿势完全相同。

senses.title: Fresh and mild in the air
senses.definition: describing weather or air that is mild, fresh and pleasant to breathe
senses.definitionCN: 形容温和、新鲜、呼吸起来舒适的气候或空气
senses.example: After the rain the hillside air felt hospitable and soft.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后的山坡空气清新而柔和。
senses.why: A branch of the same image: an airy room that lets cool air in freely is felt as hospitable to the body.
senses.whyCN: 同一意象的另一分支：让凉空气自由进来的通透居室，会被身体感受为舒适宜人。

senses.title: Luxurious by generous welcome
senses.definition: describing generous and comfortable surroundings, as in some older prose
senses.definitionCN: 形容宽敞舒适、风格豪放的环境，旧时文字中可见
senses.example: They lived in a hospitable old house with wide cool rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在一座宽敞凉爽的旧宅里。
senses.why: Generosity still rings in the older adjectival use that the word once carried for generous and ample surroundings.
senses.whyCN: 这个词旧时曾指慷慨宽裕的环境，如今这种用法里仍能听见「慷慨」的回响。

intro.en: Hospitable comes from Latin hospitabilis, formed on hospes, which means both host and guest.
intro.cn: hospitable 来自拉丁语 hospitabilis，由 hospes 构成，而 hospes 兼有「主人」与「客人」两义。

items.en: The element ghostis means stranger or guest, a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 其中 ghostis 意为「外来者、客人」，为重构形式。

items.en: Hospes means both host and guest, bound by a mutual duty of welcome.
items.cn: 拉丁语 hospes 兼指主人与客人，双方受互相款待的义务所约束。

items.en: Hospitabilis means fond of entertaining guests.
items.cn: hospitabilis 意为好客的、乐于款待客人的。

items.en: Hospitable passes through French into English, carrying the hospitality sense.
items.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，带着好客的含义。

items.en: Hospitable is recorded for a welcoming host, and later for places that suit life.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪开始记录 hospitable 形容好客的主人，后来也用于形容适宜生活的地方。

note.en: Hospitable shares the Latin hospes family with hospitality, hospital and hostel, and sits near words for warmth.
note.cn: hospitable 与 hospitality、hospital、hostel 同出拉丁语 hospes 一族，并与表示热忱的词语相邻。

entries.definition: a place where sick people receive care
entries.definitionCN: 医院；原指接待客人的房舍

entries.definition: a cheap place offering temporary lodging
entries.definitionCN: 旅舍；招待所

entries.definition: making people feel happy to arrive

entries.definition: giving freely to others

normalIntro.en: Hospitable is the hospitality family; every member traces back to Latin hospes, host and guest at once.
normalIntro.cn: hospitable 属于「款待」一族，所有成员都追溯到拉丁语 hospes，它同时指主人与客人。

normal.en: The noun hospitality names the quality, so hospitable is the adjective of that quality.
normal.cn: 名词 hospitality 指这种品质，hospitable 就是这种品质的形容词。

normal.en: Hospital comes from the same root, though its old meaning of a lodging for guests has narrowed to medical care.
normal.cn: hospital 同出这一词根，只是它原本「接待客人的房舍」之义收窄到了医疗照护。

normal.en: The opposite is formed with the negative prefix in-, giving inhospitable.
normal.cn: 加上否定前缀 in- 就得到反义词 inhospitable。

normal.en: An adverb ending in -ly, hospitably, describes how someone welcomes others.
normal.cn: 以 -ly 结尾的副词 hospitably 描述一个人迎接他人的方式。

normal.en: The pair host and guest hides inside the root, which is why the word covers both sides of the door.
normal.cn: 词根里藏着 host 与 guest 这一对，所以这个词涵盖了门的里外两边。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden door held open while a stranger steps in from the rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇木门被扶着敞开，一位陌生人在雨中走进来。

abstract.en: Imagine a long table by the village gate with bowls of soup for travellers.
abstract.cn: 想象村口摆着长桌，桌上放着给旅人的热汤。

abstract.en: Think of a green valley that accepts seeds and grows trees without being asked.
abstract.cn: 想象一片绿色山谷，不用开口就接纳种子长出树木。

examples.en: Our hosts were hospitable and made us feel at home.
examples.cn: 主人热情好客，让我们宾至如归。

examples.en: The town has a hospitable climate for growing citrus.
examples.cn: 这个小镇的气候适宜种植柑橘。

examples.en: Small villages along the coast are famous for their hospitable people.
examples.cn: 沿海的小村庄以居民好客而闻名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「好斯必特」——主人待客「好」，把客人「斯文有礼」地请进屋里；也可记作「好施」——乐于施予。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 原始印欧语重构形式 ghostis（外来者、客人）→ 拉丁语 hospes（主人兼客人）→ hospitabilis（好客的）→ 经法语进入英语，核心义「把外来者当客人好好款待」。

sensesIntro.en: Hospitable starts with welcoming guests, spreads to strangers, then transfers its warmth to places, ideas and even data.
sensesIntro.cn: hospitable 从款待客人起步，扩展到对待陌生人，再把这份热情转移到地方、想法乃至数据上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open door with a host standing by it.
core.cn: 核心意象：敞开的门，主人站在旁边迎客。

branches.en: The guest sense widens from invited friends to anyone new.
branches.cn: 客人义从受邀的朋友扩展到任何初来的人。

branches.en: The welcoming gesture moves onto land and air that receive life easily.
branches.cn: 迎客的姿态转移到能轻松接纳生命的大地与空气上。

branches.en: Ideas and criticism are let in as guests are let in.
branches.cn: 想法和批评像客人一样被请进门内。

branches.en: Digital tools borrow the same welcome for easy access to data.
branches.cn: 数字工具也借用这份欢迎感，表示数据易于获取。

branches.en: Both the guest and the generous house point back to generous, ample welcome.
branches.cn: 待客与宽适的宅屋都指向慷慨充裕的欢迎。

intro.en: Hospitable is built on the Latin host and guest root hosp-, with English adjective endings and a ready-made negative.
intro.cn: hospitable 建立在拉丁语「主人兼客人」词根 hosp- 之上，配有英语形容词词尾，并已形成现成的否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin hospes means both host and guest, and hospitabilis means welcoming.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 hospes 兼指主人与客人，hospitabilis 意为好客的。

items.example: The root hosp- carries the whole family of words.
items.exampleCN: 词根 hosp- 撑起整个词族。

items.example: Hospes binds welcome and being welcomed.
items.exampleCN: hospes 把「款待」与「被款待」绑在一起。

items.example: The suffix -able makes an adjective from the root.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 把词根变成形容词。

items.example: The prefix in- gives inhospitable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成 inhospitable。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms hospitality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 hospitality。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms hospitably.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 hospitably。

items.example: The suffix -al forms hospital from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 由同一词根构成 hospital。

items.meaning: the form seen in hostel and hotel
items.meaningCN: hostel 与 hotel 中出现的拼写形态
items.example: The spelling -ost appears in hostel and hotel.
items.exampleCN: 拼写 -ost 出现在 hostel 与 hotel 中。
