热情地；好客地
不好客的；条件恶劣的

definition_zh: 好客；热情款待；招待；餐饮住宿业
definition_en: friendly and generous treatment of guests, and the business of providing food and lodging for travellers
core_image: 主人推开家门，把客人迎进灯火通明的屋里
scene: 客人在院子里停下脚步，主人立刻接过行李，把他们领进客厅。The family showed great hospitality to the guests who arrived after midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 hospitality 是「好客、热情款待」（第 1 个义项：对客人的友善慷慨招待）；句意：这家人对半夜才到的客人非常热情。

derivatives.zh: 由名词加 -able 构成形容词，义为「好客的；宜人的」
与 hospitality 同源于「客人」之根，古义为收容朝圣者与陌生人的客舍，后专指医院
形容词 hospitable 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「好客地；盛情地」

senses.title: Friendly treatment of guests
senses.definition: kind and generous behaviour towards people who visit your home or your country
senses.definitionCN: 对来家中或本国的人给予的友善慷慨的对待
senses.example: They thanked us for our hospitality with a gift.
senses.exampleCN: 他们送了一份礼物来感谢我们的热情款待。
senses.why: The Latin stem hospes meant both host and guest, so the noun named the duty of welcoming a stranger.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词干 hospes 同时指主人与客人，所以这个词名词化后就是「迎接外来者的本分」。

senses.title: The business of hosting travellers
senses.definition: the industry of providing accommodation, food, and services to paying guests
senses.definitionCN: 向付费客人提供住宿、餐饮与服务的行业
senses.example: She works in the hospitality sector in a large city.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一座大城市的酒店餐饮业工作。
senses.why: The old duty of sheltering a stranger turned into a paid service, and the same word now names that trade.
senses.whyCN: 收留陌生人的古旧义务变成了有偿服务，同一个词就用来命名这门行当。

senses.title: A welcoming place
senses.definition: the quality of a place that makes visitors feel comfortable and welcome
senses.definitionCN: 让来访者感到舒适与受欢迎的环境特质
senses.example: The village is famous for the hospitality of its café.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子因它的咖啡馆待人亲切而出名。
senses.why: The warmth once shown by a host can be felt in a building itself, so the word extends from person to place.
senses.whyCN: 主人身上的热情被人从建筑里感受到，词语便从人延伸到了场所。

intro.en: Hospitality comes from Latin hospitalitas, the treatment given to guests, built on hospes, which meant both host and guest.
intro.cn: hospitality 来自拉丁语 hospitalitas（待客之道），词根 hospes 同时表示主人与客人。

items.en: Hospes means both host and guest, a stranger bound by the custom of guest-friendship.
items.cn: hospes 既指主人也指客人，指受客谊习俗约束的陌生人。

items.en: Hospitalitas means the practice of welcoming guests.
items.cn: hospitalitas 意为接待客人的做法。

items.en: Hospitalite carries the idea of kindly treatment of visitors into French.
items.cn: hospitalite 把善待访客的观念带入法语。

items.en: Hospitality enters English with the sense of the duty of a host.
items.cn: hospitality 以「主人之责」的含义进入英语。

items.en: The word spreads into trade names for hotels, restaurants, and tourism.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词扩展到酒店、餐厅与旅游的行业名称。

note.en: Hospitality belongs to the family of hospital and hospitable, and sits beside words about welcoming guests.
note.cn: hospitality 属于 hospital、hospitable 一族，与表示「待客」的词相邻。

entries.definition: a place where sick people are cared for
entries.definitionCN: 与 hospitality 同根，原指收容陌生人的客舍，现指医院

entries.definition: friendly to guests
entries.definitionCN: 好客的；宜人的

entries.definition: a cheap place for travellers to sleep
entries.definitionCN: 与 hospitality 同源于拉丁 hostis，指便宜的旅舍

entries.definition: a kind greeting given to a visitor
entries.definitionCN: 欢迎；迎接

entries.definition: the habit of giving freely
entries.definitionCN: 慷慨；大方

entries.definition: polite behaviour towards others
entries.definitionCN: 礼貌；殷勤

normalIntro.en: Hospitality is built from the old guest word hospes, the same stem that gave hospital and hostel.
normalIntro.cn: hospitality 由古老的「客人」词 hospes 构成，与 hospital、hostel 同源。

normal.en: Hospitable is the adjective, so a hospitable family offers hospitality.
normal.cn: hospitable 是它的形容词，好客的一家人提供的就是 hospitality。

normal.en: The hospitality industry covers hotels, restaurants, and tourism.
normal.cn: the hospitality industry 涵盖酒店、餐厅与旅游业。

normal.en: Remember hospital: a place that once sheltered strangers now heals them.
normal.cn: 记住 hospital：它曾收留陌生人，如今治愈病人。

normal.en: To show hospitality to someone is to make a guest feel at home.
normal.cn: show hospitality to someone 就是让客人宾至如归。

normal.en: Hospitality is uncountable in daily use even though a plural form exists.
normal.cn: 虽然存在复数形式，hospitality 在日常中仍是不可数名词。

abstract.en: Picture a door held open and a light left on for a late traveller.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇被拉开的门，为迟归的旅人留着一盏灯。

abstract.en: Imagine a front desk where a tired stranger is given a warm room.
abstract.cn: 想象一张前台，疲惫的陌生人得到一间温暖的房间。

abstract.en: Think of a market stall where a shopkeeper offers tea before talking price.
abstract.cn: 想象一个摊位，店主先递上一杯茶再谈价钱。

examples.en: Thank you for your hospitality during our stay in Beijing.
examples.cn: 感谢你们在北京期间的热情款待。

examples.en: Tourism and hospitality employ thousands of people on the coast.
examples.cn: 旅游业与酒店餐饮业在沿海地区雇用了数千人。

examples.en: The small inn is known for its hospitality.
examples.cn: 这家小客栈以好客闻名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「豪死皮疼」不挨边——记成「好士披」：好客的主人给客人披上外套；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 hospes（主人兼客人，受客谊习俗约束的陌生人）→ hospitalitas（待客之道）→ 古法语 hospitalite → 英语 hospitality，核心义「把外来者当自己人招待」。

sensesIntro.en: Hospitality moves from the personal duty of a host, to the paid trade of hosting travellers, and finally to the welcoming feel of a place.
sensesIntro.cn: hospitality 从主人待客的个人本分，走向接待旅人的付费行业，最后落到场所本身的宜人气质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a host holding the door open for a guest.
core.cn: 核心意象：主人为客人把门拉开。

branches.en: Welcoming a guest is the everyday personal sense.
branches.cn: 迎接客人是日常的个人义项。

branches.en: Paid lodging turns the duty into a trade.
branches.cn: 有偿住宿把这份本分变成行业。

branches.en: A welcoming atmosphere is the sense applied to places.
branches.cn: 亲切氛围是把词义移用到场所。

branches.en: A warm host and a warm café share the same image of being received.
branches.cn: 热情的主人与热情的咖啡馆共享「被接待」的意象。

branches.en: The hotel trade grew out of the older custom of taking in travellers.
branches.cn: 酒店业脱胎于收留旅人的古老习俗。

intro.en: Hospitality is a Latin noun in -itas, built on the guest stem hospes, with siblings hospital, hostel, hotel, and host.
intro.cn: hospitality 是带 -itas 词尾的拉丁名词，词干 hospes 表示客人，同族词有 hospital、hostel、hotel 与 host。

latinIntro.en: Latin hospes named the host and the guest, and hospitium named the bond between them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 hospes 指主人与客人，hospitium 指两者之间的关系与客舍。

items.example: Hospes gave the whole word family its shape.
items.exampleCN: hospes 决定了整个词族的形态。

items.example: Hospitium named both the bond and the place.
items.exampleCN: hospitium 既指情谊也指住处。

items.example: The suffix -itas makes hospitalitas from hospitalis.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -itas 把 hospitalis 变成 hospitalitas。

items.example: Hospitality is the abstract quality of a host.
items.exampleCN: hospitality 是主人身上的抽象品质。

items.example: Hospitable keeps the same guest stem.
items.exampleCN: hospitable 保留同一个「客人」词干。

items.example: The suffix -able turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Hospital began as a shelter for guests.
items.exampleCN: hospital 最初指接待客人的场所。

items.example: Hostel keeps the lodging sense.
items.exampleCN: hostel 保留了住宿的含义。

items.example: Hotel is the French spelling of the same root.
items.exampleCN: hotel 是同一词根的拼法。

definition_zh: 青年旅舍；廉价旅舍；学生宿舍；收容所
definition_en: a cheap place where travellers or students can stay the night, often sharing rooms
core_image: 山路尽头一栋小楼，灯亮着，旅人推门找到一张空床
scene: 背包客错过了末班车，只好在车站附近住下。The young travellers stayed in a cheap hostel near the station.
sceneCN: 这里 hostel 是「青年旅舍、廉价旅舍」（第 1 个义项：供旅人便宜住宿的地方）；句意：年轻旅人住在一家车站附近的廉价旅舍。

pos.zh: 青年旅舍；廉价旅舍；学生宿舍；收容所

derivatives.zh: 由 hostel 加 -er 构成，义为「住青年旅舍的人」
hostel 加 -ry 构成，古旧说法，义为「客栈；旅店业」
动词 hostel 加 -ing 构成动名词，义为「住青年旅舍」，多用于英式说法

senses.title: A cheap lodging for travellers
senses.definition: a simple place with cheap beds, often shared, where young or budget travellers stay
senses.definitionCN: 床位便宜、常为合住的简易住所，供年轻或节省的旅人居住
senses.example: We booked a hostel with a shared kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 我们订了一家带共用厨房的青年旅舍。
senses.why: The Latin word for a guest passed through Old French and named a place that takes in travellers.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示「客人」的词经古法语传来，用来指收留旅人的场所。

senses.title: Student accommodation
senses.definition: a building where students live during their studies
senses.definitionCN: 学生在求学期间居住的楼舍
senses.example: Many freshmen move into the hostel in their first week.
senses.exampleCN: 许多大一新生在第一周就搬进学生宿舍。
senses.why: A place that shelters strangers for the night easily becomes a place that shelters students for a year.
senses.whyCN: 收留陌生人过夜的地方，自然变成收留学生一年的住所。

senses.title: A place that shelters the needy
senses.definition: a place run by a charity or city for homeless or poor people to sleep
senses.definitionCN: 由慈善机构或市政开办、供无家可归者或穷人过夜的地方
senses.example: The hostel offers meals and a bed for the night.
senses.exampleCN: 这家收容所提供一顿饭和一张过夜的床。
senses.why: The oldest meaning of the root was shelter for strangers, and that charitable sense survives for those in need.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根最古老的意思就是收留陌生人，这份慈善意味留在给困苦者的收容义上。

intro.en: Hostel comes from Old French hostel, from Latin hospitale, a guest room, a relative of hospital and hotel.
intro.cn: hostel 来自古法语 hostel，源于拉丁语 hospitale（客房），与 hospital、hotel 同族。

items.en: Hospitale is a guest chamber, built on hospes, the host or guest.
items.cn: hospitale 指客房，来自 hospes（主人或客人）。

items.en: Hostel means a lodging house where travellers stop.
items.cn: hostel 意为旅人投宿的客舍。

items.en: Hostel names an inn in English, while hospital keeps the care sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 hostel 指客栈，而 hospital 保留照料病人的含义。

items.en: Hotel is borrowed from French and slowly replaces hostel for the inn.
items.cn: hotel 从法语借入，逐渐取代 hostel 表示高档旅馆。

items.en: Hostel finds a new life as the cheap youth hostel for walkers and students.
items.cn: hostel 在青年旅舍这一新生事物上重获生机。

note.en: Hostel shares the guest root with hospital, hotel, and hospitality, and sits beside lodging words.
note.cn: hostel 与 hospital、hotel、hospitality 同源于「客人」，并与各种住宿词相邻。

entries.definition: a building with paid rooms for guests
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，指付费入住的旅馆，档次通常高于 hostel

entries.definition: a place that treats sick people
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，原义为收容客人的房舍，现指医院

entries.definition: unfriendly feeling
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，但来自表示「敌人」的拉丁 hostis，义为敌意，与 hostel 含义不同

entries.definition: a small old-fashioned hotel with food
entries.definitionCN: 小客栈；乡村旅店

entries.definition: a room or building with many beds
entries.definitionCN: 集体宿舍

entries.definition: a small private house for paying guests
entries.definitionCN: 私人经营的小旅舍

normalIntro.en: Hostel is the cheap cousin of hotel: same guest root, older spelling, lower price.
normalIntro.cn: hostel 是 hotel 的平价表亲：同样来自「客人」词根，拼法更老，价钱更低。

normal.en: Drop the e from hotel and you have hostel.
normal.cn: 把 hotel 的 e 去掉，就成了 hostel。

normal.en: A youth hostel is meant for young walkers with small budgets.
normal.cn: youth hostel 是给预算有限的年轻徒步者的住处。

normal.en: Hospital, hotel, hostel, and hospitality all begin with host.
normal.cn: hospital、hotel、hostel、hospitality 都以 host 起头。

normal.en: Hostel beds are often shared, so silence is a shared duty.
normal.cn: 旅舍床位常为合住，保持安静是大家共同的义务。

normal.en: In British student talk, the hostel means university housing.
normal.cn: 在英式学生口语里，the hostel 指大学提供的宿舍。

abstract.en: Picture a bunk bed with a rucksack hanging from the rail.
abstract.cn: 想象一张上下铺，栏杆上挂着一只背包。

abstract.en: Imagine a hallway of doors where each number is a student name.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊，每扇门后是一个学生的名字。

abstract.en: Think of a warm lamp above a bench where a night guard hands out blankets.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长椅上方亮着暖灯，夜里有人发着毯子。

examples.en: The hostel had a shared kitchen and a small garden.
examples.cn: 这家旅舍有一个共用厨房和一个小花园。

examples.en: She stayed in youth hostels during her trip across Europe.
examples.cn: 她在环游欧洲时住的都是青年旅舍。

examples.en: New students can apply for a room in the hostel.
examples.cn: 新生可以申请学生宿舍的房间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「好事的」——住青年旅舍总遇到各种奇闻「好事的」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 hospes / hospitale（客人、客房）→ 古法语 hostel（客舍）→ 中古英语 hostel → 现代英语「青年旅舍；宿舍」，核心义「给旅人一张便宜的床」。

sensesIntro.en: Hostel begins as a cheap bed for travellers, shifts to shared housing for students, and keeps the charitable sense of shelter for the needy.
sensesIntro.cn: hostel 先是给旅人的便宜床位，再转为学生合住宿舍，并保留收留困苦者的慈善义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit window at the end of a mountain road.
core.cn: 核心意象：山路尽头亮着灯的一扇窗。

branches.en: A cheap bed for travellers is the core sense.
branches.cn: 给旅人的便宜床位是核心义项。

branches.en: Shared rooms for students is the institutional sense.
branches.cn: 学生合住宿舍是机构化义项。

branches.en: Shelter for the needy is the charitable sense.
branches.cn: 收留困苦者是慈善义项。

branches.en: Both a traveller and a student need a cheap shared room.
branches.cn: 旅人与学生都需要一间便宜的合住房。

branches.en: A dorm bed and a city shelter both answer the need for one night.
branches.cn: 宿舍床与收容床位都回应「过一夜」的需要。

intro.en: Hostel is a blunt noun with almost no affix, but the guest root hosp- links it to hospital, hotel, and hospitality.
intro.cn: hostel 本身几乎不带词缀，但「客人」词根 hosp- 把它与 hospital、hotel、hospitality 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin hospes means host or guest, and hospitale means a guest room.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 hospes 指主人或客人，hospitale 指客房。

items.example: Hospes is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: hospes 是整个词族的根。

items.example: Hospitale is the direct source of hostel and hotel.
items.exampleCN: hospitale 是 hostel 与 hotel 的直接来源。

items.example: Hostel keeps the lodging sense of the root.
items.exampleCN: hostel 保留词根的住宿含义。

items.example: Hotel is the modern French form of the same word.
items.exampleCN: hotel 是同一个词的现代法语形式。

items.example: Hospital splits off to name a place of care.
items.exampleCN: hospital 分化出去表示照料之所。

items.example: Hospitality names the quality, not the building.
items.exampleCN: hospitality 命名品质而非建筑。

items.meaning: a person staying at a hostel
items.example: The agent noun -er forms hosteller.
items.exampleCN: 施事后缀 -er 构成 hosteller。

items.meaningCN: 表示场所或行业的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ry forms hostelry, an old word for inns.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ry 构成 hostelry，即旧称的客栈。

definition_zh: 敌意；敌视；敌对行为；战争状态
definition_en: strong unfriendly feeling towards someone, and actions or open conflict that show it
core_image: 两人隔着一道门，各自握紧拳头不肯先松手
scene: 谈判桌上双方互不相让，房间里气氛越来越冷。Hostility between the two neighbours broke out into open argument.
sceneCN: 这里 hostility 是「敌意、敌视」（第 1 个义项：强烈的不友善情绪）；句意：两家邻居之间的敌意爆发成了公开的争吵。

pos.zh: 敌意；敌视；敌对行为；战争状态

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 hostilis 来的形容词，义为「敌对的；不友善的；不利的」
形容词 hostile 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「敌对地」
由 hostile 加 -ize 构成，义为「使产生敌意」，较少使用

senses.title: Unfriendly feeling
senses.definition: a strong feeling of dislike or unfriendliness towards someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人强烈的不喜欢或不友善情绪
senses.example: There was open hostility in her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的话音里带着毫不掩饰的敌意。
senses.why: The Latin root hostis means enemy, so the noun simply names the feeling an enemy stirs.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 hostis 就是「敌人」，这个词于是直接命名敌人带来的情绪。

senses.title: Hostile acts
senses.definition: actions intended to hurt, block, or oppose someone
senses.definitionCN: 旨在伤害、阻挠或反对某人的行为
senses.example: The workers met the new rules with hostility.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们对新规定报以对抗态度。
senses.why: Feeling turns into action, so the word also covers the gestures and steps an enemy takes.
senses.whyCN: 情绪转化为行动，这个词便也涵盖敌人做出的小动作与举措。

senses.title: State of war
senses.definition: open fighting between countries or groups, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 国家或团体之间公开的武装冲突，通常用复数
senses.example: Both sides agreed to end hostilities.
senses.exampleCN: 双方同意停止交战。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the enemy root is armed conflict, which survives in the plural hostilities.
senses.whyCN: 表示「敌人」的词根最古老的意思是武装冲突，复数 hostilities 保留了这层。

intro.en: Hostility comes from Latin hostilitas, from hostilis, enemy, built on hostis, a stranger or enemy, the same root as host and hostile.
intro.cn: hostility 来自拉丁语 hostilitas，源于 hostilis（敌人的），词根 hostis 指陌生人或敌人，与 host、hostile 同源。

items.en: Hostis first means a foreigner and later a foe in war.
items.cn: hostis 最初指外国人，后来指战争中的敌人。

items.en: Hostilitas means open enmity and the conditions of war.
items.cn: hostilitas 意为公开的敌意与战争状态。

items.en: Hostilite arrives in French with the sense of war rather than personal anger.
items.cn: hostilite 进入法语时更多指战争状态而非个人怒气。

items.en: Hostility is used in English for acts of war and for enmity.
items.cn: 中古英语里 hostility 既指战争行为也指敌意。

items.en: Personal unfriendliness becomes the dominant sense, while the plural keeps the war sense.
items.cn: 现代英语中个人层面的不友善成为主流，复数形式保留战争义。

note.en: Hostility has the enemy root hostis, shared with hostile and host in the service sense, and sits beside words for dislike and conflict.
note.cn: hostility 带着表示敌人的 hostis 词根，与 hostile、以及服务业的 host 同源，与各种表示厌恶与冲突的词相邻。

entries.definition: unfriendly or ready to fight
entries.definitionCN: hostility 的形容词形式，义为「敌对的；不友善的」

entries.definition: a cheap lodging
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同：来自表示客人的词组，与敌意无关

entries.definition: a person who receives guests
entries.definitionCN: 同源于拉丁 hostis（陌生人、主人），义为「主人；东道主」

entries.definition: a deep feeling of hatred between people
entries.definitionCN: 长期深层的敌意；仇恨

entries.definition: a strong feeling of anger and dislike
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的恼怒与厌恶

entries.definition: active opposition rather than feeling
entries.definitionCN: 公开的对立与反对

normalIntro.en: Hostility grows from hostis, the Latin enemy, so every hostile word carries an old foe inside it.
normalIntro.cn: hostility 生自拉丁语的敌人 hostis，每个带 hostile 的说法里都藏着一个旧日对手。

normal.en: The adjective hostile, not hostily, is the common partner of the noun.
normal.cn: 与这个名词最常搭配的是形容词 hostile。

normal.en: Hostilities in the plural usually means fighting in war.
normal.cn: 复数 hostilities 通常指战争中的交火。

normal.en: Host is the person or machine, hostile is the mood, hostility is the mood made into a noun.
normal.cn: host 是人或机器，hostile 是情绪，hostility 是把这份情绪名词化。

normal.en: Compare hostel: it looks similar but comes from a guest word, not an enemy word.
normal.cn: 对比 hostel：拼写相近，但它来自「客人」而非「敌人」。

normal.en: To show hostility towards a newcomer is to treat them as an intruder.
normal.cn: show hostility towards a newcomer 就是把新来者当外人。

abstract.en: Picture two people on opposite sides of a table, arms crossed.
abstract.cn: 想象两人隔桌对坐，都抱着胳膊。

abstract.en: Imagine a border gate where soldiers glare at each other.
abstract.cn: 想象一道边境关卡，两边士兵互相瞪视。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd that turns silent and folds its arms the moment a speaker walks on.
abstract.cn: 想象演讲者一上台，全场立刻沉默并抱起双臂。

examples.en: He felt no hostility towards his old rival.
examples.cn: 他对昔日的对手已毫无敌意。

examples.en: The plan met with hostility from local residents.
examples.cn: 这项计划遭到当地居民的抵制。

examples.en: Fighting stopped when hostilities ceased at dawn.
examples.cn: 黎明时分战事停止，交火随之结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「好死缇勒」——「好死都不理他」是十足的敌意；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 hostis（陌生人；敌人）→ hostilis（敌人的）→ hostilitas（敌意、战争状态）→ 古法语 hostilite → 英语 hostility，核心义「把人当敌人」。

sensesIntro.en: Hostility starts as the feeling an enemy stirs, passes into the acts that show it, and finally names open war.
sensesIntro.cn: hostility 先是敌人激起的那种情绪，再落到表现这种情绪的行为，最后指向公开的战争。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two fists held tight across a closed door.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人隔着一道紧闭的门，各自握紧拳头。

branches.en: Unfriendly feeling is the psychological sense.
branches.cn: 不友善的情绪是心理义项。

branches.en: Acts of opposition are the behavioural sense.
branches.cn: 对抗的行为是行为义项。

branches.en: Open war is the collective sense kept in the plural.
branches.cn: 公开战争是保留在复数里的集合义项。

branches.en: Inner anger often shows itself in concrete acts of blocking and refusal.
branches.cn: 内心的怒气常以阻挠与拒绝的具体行为显现。

branches.en: Acts of hostility on a large scale become hostilities at the front.
branches.cn: 当敌对行为扩大成规模，就成了前线的交战。

intro.en: Hostility is the noun of the -ility type built on hostilis, enemy, with hostile as its adjective.
intro.cn: hostility 是加 -ility 类词尾的名词，来自 hostilis（敌人的），形容词是 hostile。

latinIntro.en: Latin hostis means stranger or enemy, and hostilitas means enmity or war.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 hostis 指陌生人或敌人，hostilitas 指敌意或战争。

items.example: Hostis is the shared root of hostile and hostility.
items.exampleCN: hostis 是 hostile 与 hostility 的共同词根。

items.example: Hostilis feeds both the English adjective and the noun.
items.exampleCN: hostilis 同时滋养英语的形容词与名词。

items.example: The suffix -itas forms hostilitas from hostilis.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -itas 把 hostilis 变成 hostilitas。

items.example: Hostility keeps the quality sense.
items.exampleCN: hostility 保留性质名词的用法。

items.example: Hostile drops the noun ending.
items.exampleCN: hostile 省去了名词词尾。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb hostilely.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成副词 hostilely。

items.example: The plural hostilities names acts of war.
items.exampleCN: 复数 hostilities 指战争行为。

items.meaning: a host, an army, a receiver of guests
items.example: Host keeps the older stranger sense of the root.
items.exampleCN: host 保留了词根较古老的「外人」含义。

items.example: Hospitable flips the enemy root into welcome.
items.exampleCN: hospitable 把「敌人」词根翻成了欢迎。

definition_zh: 实习医生；驻院内科医生；旅馆勤杂工；房客
definition_en: a junior doctor working and living in a hospital, or a member of staff who does odd jobs in a hotel or house
core_image: 医院的走廊尽头有一间值班室，白大褂还挂在门后，年轻的医生就睡在病房隔壁
scene: 深夜的医院里，刚毕业的年轻医生住在病房隔壁的小房间里，随叫随到。After the night shift, the young houseman fell asleep in the room beside the ward.
sceneCN: 这里 houseman 是「驻院实习医生」（第 1 个义项：住在医院里、负责日常病房杂务的初级医生）；句意：值完夜班后，那位年轻的驻院医生在病房旁边的小房间里睡着了。图中可辨识物件：病房、值班室、白大褂、走廊。

pos.zh: 实习医生；驻院内科医生

collocations.zh: 驻院实习医生（正式称谓）

derivatives.zh: 由 house 与 man 复合而成，基础词义为「房屋」，也指剧院、医院等机构建筑
复合词第二成分，古英语指「人」，在现代英语助手中常带「职务、干活的人」色彩
由 house 与 keeping 构成，义为「家务；客房整理」，与旅馆勤杂工的职责相邻
由 house 与 hold 组合，义为「家庭；家户」，保留 house 的「住所」核心

senses.title: A junior doctor living in hospital
senses.definition: a young doctor who has just qualified and lives and works in a hospital while completing early training
senses.definitionCN: 刚取得资格、在完成初期培训时住在医院里、负责病房日常工作的年轻医生
senses.example: The houseman checked every patient on the ward before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 那位驻院实习医生在天亮前查完了病房里的每一位病人。
senses.why: The house of this word is the hospital building, and a man who lives in the house is the junior doctor who must stay on the spot all night.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 house 指医院大楼，住在「屋里」的人就是必须整夜守在病房旁边的初级医生，所以这个词天然带着「住进去、随时待命」的画面。

senses.title: A resident medical officer
senses.definition: a hospital doctor, usually in internal medicine, who has residential duties and stays close to the wards
senses.definitionCN: 在医院担任住院职责、通常负责内科、常在病房附近留守的医生
senses.example: She worked for two years as a medical houseman.
senses.exampleCN: 她当过两年驻院内科医生。
senses.why: Once the junior post is established, the title also names the residential physician who carries ward duties, so the house sense widens from a single job to a role.
senses.whyCN: 初级岗位稳定下来后，这个称呼也被用来指承担病房职责的驻院医生，于是「房子」的含义从一个职位扩展到一类角色。

senses.title: A hotel or household helper
senses.definition: a male servant or hotel worker who carries luggage and does small jobs around the house
senses.definitionCN: 负责搬运行李、在房屋或旅馆里干杂活的男性仆役或服务人员
senses.example: An elderly houseman carried our bags up the narrow stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 一位上了年纪的勤杂工把我们的行李搬上窄楼梯。
senses.why: Before medicine borrowed the word, houseman simply meant a servant who belongs to a house and does its work, so the core sense keeps its oldest shape here.
senses.whyCN: 在医学借用这个词之前，houseman 本义就是「属于某座房子、替它干活的人」，所以第 3 个义项保留了最古老的形态。

senses.title: A lodger in a house
senses.definition: a man who rents a room in a house owned by someone else and lives there
senses.definitionCN: 在别人家里租住一个房间、并在那里生活的男子
senses.example: The widowed landlady kept one houseman to share the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 那位寡妇房东留下一位房客来分担房租。
senses.why: The compound marks not ownership but residence, so the house can be a rented room and the man only a lodger who lives under its roof.
senses.whyCN: 复合词强调的不是产权而是居住，所以 house 可以是租来的房间，而 man 只是住在同一屋檐下的房客。

intro.en: Houseman is an English compound of house and man, plainly built and old in shape; the medical sense is a later extension borrowed from hospital life.
intro.cn: houseman 是 house 与 man 的英语复合词，构词直白、词形古老；医学义项则是后来从医院生活里延伸出来的用法。

items.en: Old English had hus meaning a dwelling and man meaning a human being, and the two words join freely in compounds.
items.cn: 古英语已有 hus（住所）与 man（人），两词在复合词里可以自由结合。

items.en: Spellings shift from hus to house, and compounds with house begin to name people who belong to a household.
items.cn: 拼写从 hus 过渡到 house，以 house 打头的复合词开始指属于某户人家的人。

items.en: Houseman is recorded in the general sense of one who lives in a house or serves in it, alongside its plural housemen.
items.cn: 十六世纪前后，houseman 已用来指「住在某屋里的人」或「在屋里做事的人」，复数 housemen 同时出现。

items.en: British hospitals name the resident junior doctor a house physician or house surgeon, and the shorter houseman soon follows.
items.cn: 十九世纪的英国医院把住在院内的初级医生称为 house physician 或 house surgeon，更短的 houseman 随后也流行起来。

items.en: Houseman becomes a standard medical grade in Britain and later fades as formal titles change, while the hotel and servant senses stay in old texts.
items.cn: 二十世纪 houseman 成为英国医院里的标准职称，后来随正式称谓改变而淡出；旅馆勤杂工与仆役义则多见于旧文本。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the house compounds with the same shape, and the near-meaning group collects the doctor and servant words whose duties overlap with houseman.
note.cn: 形近组收的是同样以 house 打头、构词相同的复合词；近义组收的是职责与 houseman 重叠的医生词与仆役词。

entries.definition: a female servant who cleans rooms and does housework, formed like houseman with a different second element
entries.definitionCN: 女佣，由 house 与 maid 复合而成，构词方式与 houseman 相同，只是第二成分不同

entries.definition: a person, usually a woman, employed to look after a house or a hotel floor
entries.definitionCN: 管家或客房主管，由 house 与 keeper 构成，同样以 house 打头

entries.definition: a teacher in charge of one boarding house at a school; the house here is a school dormitory
entries.definitionCN: 寄宿学校的舍监，这里的 house 指学校的一栋宿舍楼

entries.definition: a recent medical graduate in the first year of hospital training, near the British houseman
entries.definitionCN: 美式说法，指刚毕业、在医院接受第一年培训的医生，与英式 houseman 大致对应

entries.definition: a doctor who lives and works in a hospital during training, a wider term than houseman
entries.definitionCN: 驻院医生，泛指培训期间住在医院的医生，范围比 houseman 更宽

entries.definition: a person who runs an inn, close to the hotel worker sense of houseman
entries.definitionCN: 旅店老板或经营者，与 houseman 的旅馆勤杂工义项处在同一义场

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the literal building blocks house and man, the plural form, and the British hospital tradition.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子利用真实的构词成分 house 与 man、复数形式，以及英国医院的传统。

normal.en: House plus man is the plainest compound in English: the man who is at the house.
normal.cn: house 加 man 是英语里最直白的复合词：待在房子里的人。

normal.en: The plural changes the middle vowel: houseman becomes housemen, like man becomes men.
normal.cn: 复数变化落在中间的元音上：houseman 变 housemen，与 man 变 men 同理。

normal.en: In British hospitals the house is the ward building, so the houseman is the doctor on site all night.
normal.cn: 在英国医院里，house 指病房楼，所以 houseman 就是整夜守在院内的医生。

normal.en: The older job sense is a servant of the house, and that sense survives in old novels about hotels.
normal.cn: 较早的职业义是「替这户人家做事的仆役」，这一用法在描写旅馆的旧小说里还能见到。

normal.en: Compare house surgeon and house physician: houseman is simply their shortened everyday name.
normal.cn: 对比 house surgeon 与 house physician：houseman 只是它们更短、更口语的称呼。

abstract.en: Picture a room at the end of the ward with one narrow bed, and the young doctor asleep but on call.
abstract.cn: 想象病房尽头的一间小屋、一张窄床，年轻医生睡着，却随时会被叫醒。

abstract.en: Picture the same house-like room becoming a permanent post, so the doctor stays and the title settles.
abstract.cn: 想象同样那间像家的屋子变成一个常设岗位，医生留下来，称呼也就固定了。

abstract.en: Picture a hotel staircase: a man in a dark waistcoat carries a suitcase up, doing the house work for strangers.
abstract.cn: 想象旅馆的楼梯：穿深色马甲的男人扛着行李箱上楼，替陌生房客干着这座房子的活。

examples.en: As a houseman he rarely left the hospital for three days.
examples.cn: 作为驻院实习医生，他有三天几乎没离开过医院。

examples.en: Two housemen shared the on-call rota during the winter.
examples.cn: 冬天时有两名驻院医生轮流值守。

examples.en: The old hotel still employs a houseman to carry luggage.
examples.cn: 那家老旅馆仍雇着一位勤杂工帮忙搬行李。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「好士曼」——好一位守在医院这栋「房子」里的年轻男士；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 hus（房屋）+ man（人）→ 中古英语 house + man → 指「住在屋里或在屋里做事的人」→ 十九世纪英国医院把住院初级医生称为 house physician 或 house surgeon，缩为 houseman，核心义「依附于某栋房子、为它干活的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Houseman moves from a man who lives in or serves a house, to the junior doctor housed inside a hospital, then to the established resident physician, and finally to the lodger who only rents a room.
sensesIntro.cn: houseman 从「住在屋里或替屋子干活的人」出发，到医院里住着的初级医生、稳定的驻院内科医生，最后到只租一个房间的房客。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young doctor asleep in a small room beside the ward, ready to be called.
core.cn: 核心意象：病房旁的小屋里睡着年轻医生，随时候命。

branches.en: THE WARD: the house is a hospital building and its young tenant is the doctor.
branches.cn: 病房线：房子指医院大楼，里面的年轻住户就是医生。

branches.en: THE POST: residence turns into a lasting role with regular ward duties.
branches.cn: 岗位线：住下来变成一项长期职责，有了固定的病房工作。

branches.en: THE SERVICE: the servant of the house becomes the hotel or household helper.
branches.cn: 服务线：屋里的仆役变成旅馆或家庭的勤杂工。

branches.en: THE ROOM: the house can simply be a rented room, so the man is a lodger.
branches.cn: 房间线：房子也可以只是租来的一间房，于是人就成了房客。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of living at the place of work, which is the medical core.
branches.cn: 两个医学义项都共享「住在工作地点」这一点，这正是它们的核心。

intro.en: Houseman is built only from native English parts, house and man, so its word family is a set of house compounds rather than Latin elements.
intro.cn: houseman 完全由本族英语成分 house 与 man 构成，因此它的词族是一组以 house 打头的复合词，而不是拉丁语成分。

latinIntro.en: Neither house nor man comes from Latin, so there is no Latin family behind this compound and the related Latin words are left empty.
latinIntro.cn: house 与 man 都不来自拉丁语，所以这个复合词背后没有拉丁同源词，相关条目留空。

items.example: Old English hus is the first element of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 hus 是这个复合词的第一成分。

items.example: Man gives the compound its agent sense.
items.exampleCN: man 为复合词提供「做某事的人」这一含义。

items.meaning: a building for living in, or a place of work like a hospital
items.meaningCN: 居住的房屋；也指医院等机构建筑
items.example: House extends from a home to an institution.
items.exampleCN: house 从「家」扩展到「机构大楼」。

items.meaning: a live-in junior doctor, or a house servant
items.meaningCN: 驻院实习医生；屋里的仆役
items.example: Houseman joins the two native parts.
items.exampleCN: houseman 把两个本族词成分合在一起。

items.example: The plural ending -men forms housemen.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式 housemen 用了 -men 词尾。

items.meaning: a doctor living in a hospital
items.example: House physician is the long form behind houseman.
items.exampleCN: house physician 是 houseman 背后较长的说法。

items.meaning: a surgeon living in a hospital
items.example: House surgeon follows the same house pattern.
items.exampleCN: house surgeon 沿用同样的 house 构词模式。

items.example: Housemaid shows the same house plus worker pattern.
items.exampleCN: housemaid 展示了相同的「house 加干活者」模式。

items.meaning: a person who manages a house
items.example: Housekeeper keeps the house as its working place.
items.exampleCN: housekeeper 同样把 house 当作工作场所。

definition_zh: 盘旋；悬浮；徘徊；犹豫；动摇
definition_en: to stay in the air in one place, to stay near someone or something without moving away, or to be uncertain between two choices
core_image: 一只蜂鸟在花前鼓动翅膀，身体停在半空一动不动
scene: 花园里一只蜂鸟对着花朵扇动翅膀，好像悬在空中不肯落下来。A hummingbird hovers above the red flower, wings beating too fast to see.
sceneCN: 这里 hover 是「盘旋；悬停」（第 1 个义项：在空中停住不前进也不落下）；句意：一只蜂鸟悬停在红花上方，翅膀快得看不清。图中可辨识物件：蜂鸟、红花、翅膀、半空的空气。

collocations.zh: 在……上方停留；也指鼠标悬停在图标上
在某一水平上徘徊浮动

derivatives.zh: 由 hover 与 craft 复合而成，义为「气垫船」，靠气流在船底把船托离水面
由 hover 与 board 复合而成，义为「悬浮滑板」，借「悬停」画面造的现代词
由现在分词转为形容词，义为「悬停的；盘旋的；徘徊不去的」
由 hover 加 -er 构成，义为「在旁边徘徊不去的人」

senses.title: To stay in the air in one place
senses.definition: to stay in the air above one place, moving the wings but not moving forward or landing
senses.definitionCN: 停在一处上空，翅膀不停动作却不前进也不落下
senses.example: A hawk hovered above the field before it dropped.
senses.exampleCN: 一只鹰在田野上方盘旋，随后俯冲下来。
senses.why: The word names a body that is held in one spot without support, so the base picture is a bird or insect beating its wings and staying still overhead.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指身体没有任何支撑却停在同一个位置，所以最基础的画面就是鸟或昆虫振动翅膀、悬在头顶不走。

senses.title: To float or levitate
senses.definition: to be lifted above a surface and to stay there, as a helicopter or a machine does
senses.definitionCN: 被托离表面并停留在那里，如直升机或机器所做的那样
senses.example: The drone hovers steadily just above the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 那架无人机稳稳地悬停在屋顶上方。
senses.why: A machine copies the bird: rotors push air down and the craft is held in one place, so the hovering picture moves from living wings to engines.
senses.whyCN: 机器照搬了鸟的做法：旋翼把空气往下推，机身停在一点，于是「悬停」的画面从活翅膀转移到了发动机上。

senses.title: To linger nearby
senses.definition: to stay close to a person or place without leaving, often waiting for something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 守在人或者地方附近不肯离开，常指等着某事发生
senses.example: Reporters hovered outside the courtroom all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们在法庭外徘徊了一整个上午。
senses.why: Someone who does not advance and does not depart is doing on foot what a bird does overhead, so hover grows into a word for lingering near a place.
senses.whyCN: 既不前进也不离开的人，在地面上做的正是鸟儿在空中做的事，于是 hover 长出了「在地点旁边逗留」的含义。

senses.title: To be about to do something
senses.definition: to be very close to happening or to be on the point of an action
senses.definitionCN: 非常接近发生，或者正处于某个动作的临界状态
senses.example: A storm hovered over the valley for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 一场暴风雨在山谷上空盘桓了好几个小时。
senses.why: Keeping still above a target is what a hawk does before it drops, so to hover comes to mean to hang just before a decisive move.
senses.whyCN: 鹰在扑下来之前会停在目标上方不动，于是 hover 也指「处在决定性动作之前的悬置状态」。

senses.title: To be undecided
senses.definition: to be uncertain and unable to choose or settle in one direction
senses.definitionCN: 拿不准，无法作出选择，也无法定在一个方向上
senses.example: She hovered between the two offers for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 她在两份聘书之间犹豫了一个星期。
senses.why: The mind that stays between two places is balanced like a hovering bird, so the physical image becomes a picture of hesitation.
senses.whyCN: 心思停在两处之间，就像悬停的鸟一样失去方向，于是身体画面变成了犹豫的心理画面。

senses.title: To move the pointer over a screen
senses.definition: to move a computer mouse so that the pointer stays over an area of the screen without clicking
senses.definitionCN: 移动鼠标，使指针停在屏幕的某个区域上而不点击
senses.example: Hover over the image to see a larger version.
senses.exampleCN: 把鼠标悬停在图片上就能看到更大的版本。
senses.why: A pointer held still above one item waits there while the page answers, which is a small electronic copy of a bird hanging in the air.
senses.whyCN: 指针停在某个图标上方不动，等待页面回应，这几乎就是鸟儿悬在空中那一幕的电子翻版。

senses.title: To remain at a level
senses.definition: to stay around a level or figure without rising or falling much
senses.definitionCN: 停留在某个水平或数值附近，没有明显升降
senses.example: Unemployment hovered around five percent for months.
senses.exampleCN: 失业率有好几个月徘徊在百分之五左右。
senses.why: Numbers that neither climb nor drop behave like a bird that neither lands nor flies away, so hover enters the language of statistics.
senses.whyCN: 既不上升也不下降的数字，就像既不落地也不飞走的鸟，于是 hover 走进了统计与数据的说法里。

intro.en: Hover is a Middle English word for a body hanging or resting in one place; its deeper ancestry is usually linked to Old English hover meaning to remain seated or squatting, though the exact chain is not certain.
intro.cn: hover 是中古英语词，本指身体悬停或停在一处；更早的来源一般认为与古英语表示「坐着不动、蹲着」的词有关，但确切环节并不确定。

items.en: The verb hover is recorded in Old English in the sense of to remain seated or to squat, and is usually taken as the ancestor of modern hover; the link is probable rather than certain.
items.cn: 古英语中已有动词 hover，意为「坐着不动、蹲着」，一般认为它就是现代 hover 的前身；这一环节属「很可能」而非定论。

items.en: Middle English hoven and hoveren describe the act of hanging or resting in one spot, and the word begins to attach to birds and floating things.
items.cn: 中古英语的 hoven 与 hoveren 表示「停在一处、悬着」，这个词开始与鸟和漂浮之物联系起来。

items.en: Hover takes the modern spelling and is applied to hawks and insects that stay in the air over a spot.
items.cn: 十五至十六世纪，hover 定下现代拼写，并用于指停在某处上方的鹰与昆虫。

items.en: The word widens to people who linger near a place, and to uncertain or changing conditions that hang over something.
items.cn: 十七至十八世纪，词义扩展到「在地方附近逗留的人」，也用于悬在事物之上的不确定或动荡情形。

items.en: Hover enters technology, naming helicopters and drones that stay aloft, computer pointers that rest on the screen, and figures that stay near one level.
items.cn: 现代英语里，hover 进入科技领域，指悬停的直升机与无人机、停在屏幕上的鼠标指针，以及徘徊在某一水平附近的数字。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words of similar spelling or the same hanging image, and the near-meaning group collects verbs for staying, floating, or hesitating.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的词和同样带「悬着」画面的词；近义组收表示停留、漂浮与犹豫的动词。

entries.definition: a vehicle that travels over water or land on a cushion of air, formed directly from hover
entries.definitionCN: 气垫船，靠气垫浮在水面上行驶，直接由 hover 加 craft 构成

entries.definition: a board that is said to float above the ground, built from hover and board
entries.definitionCN: 悬浮滑板，由 hover 与 board 复合而成，同样取「浮在表面之上」之意

entries.definition: a fly that stays still in the air as it feeds, named straight after the hover action
entries.definitionCN: 食蚜蝇，取食时会停在半空中，名字直接来自 hover 这个动作

entries.definition: to rest or move on the surface of a liquid or in the air, supported rather than held still
entries.definitionCN: 漂在液面或空中，重点在被托住而非停住不动

entries.definition: to stay somewhere longer than expected, close to the sense of hovering near a place
entries.definitionCN: 逗留得比预想更久，与 hover 的「在附近徘徊」义项相近

entries.definition: to be unsteady in purpose and move between decisions, close to the hovering of a hesitant mind
entries.definitionCN: 心意不决、在两可之间摇动，与 hover 表示犹豫的义项相近

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Middle English forms, the preposition patterns, and the modern compounds that carry the hover action.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的中古英语词形、介词搭配模式，以及延续 hover 动作的现代复合词。

normal.en: The old verb meant to sit or squat still, and stillness in one spot is still the heart of hover.
normal.cn: 这个古老的动词本指坐着或蹲着不动，而「停在一点不动」至今仍是 hover 的核心。

normal.en: Hover regularly pairs with above and over, which mark the position just above a thing.
normal.cn: hover 常与 above、over 连用，这两个介词正好标出「在……正上方」的位置。

normal.en: Hover between marks hesitation, because between is the point of not choosing either side.
normal.cn: hover between 表示犹豫，因为 between 正是「两边都不选」的位置。

normal.en: Hovercraft and hoverboard show how the word builds machines that stay above a surface.
normal.cn: hovercraft 与 hoverboard 说明这个词怎样造出「浮在表面上」的机器。

normal.en: On a computer the pointer hovers: it rests over an icon and waits without clicking.
normal.cn: 在电脑上指针会「悬停」：停在图标上等待，却不点击。

abstract.en: Picture a hummingbird fixed in front of a flower, its body still while the wings are a blur.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蜂鸟定在花前，身体纹丝不动，翅膀却模糊成一片。

abstract.en: Picture the bird replaced by rotors: a helicopter hangs over the same roof without touching it.
abstract.cn: 想象把鸟换成旋翼：直升机悬在同一片屋顶上方，却不碰屋顶。

abstract.en: Picture a figure at the edge of a doorway, half in the room and half out, unwilling to enter or leave.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在门口，半身在屋里半身在屋外，既不进去也不离开。

examples.en: Dragonflies hover above the pond in the late afternoon.
examples.cn: 傍晚时分蜻蜓在池塘上方盘旋。

examples.en: He hovered by the door, unsure whether to knock.
examples.cn: 他在门口徘徊，拿不准要不要敲门。

examples.en: Prices have hovered near their highest level all summer.
examples.cn: 整个夏天价格一直徘徊在最高水平附近。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈弗」——想象一架飞得很慢的无人机悬在头顶，你只好仰头喊一句哈弗；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 hover（坐着不动、蹲着，一般认为与现代 hover 同源，确切环节存疑）→ 中古英语 hoven、hoveren（悬着、停在一处）→ 现代英语 hover，核心义「身体停在一点、不落地也不离开」。

sensesIntro.en: Hover begins with a body held still in the air, passes to machines that do the same, then to people who linger nearby, to something about to happen, and finally to the mind, the mouse pointer, and a level of figures.
sensesIntro.cn: hover 从「身体停在半空」出发，转到同样悬停的机器，再到在旁边逗留的人、即将发生的事，最后延伸到心思的犹豫、鼠标指针与数据的徘徊。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hummingbird beating its wings while its body stays in one place above a flower.
core.cn: 核心意象：蜂鸟振动翅膀，身体却停在花前的一点。

branches.en: THE BIRD: wings move but the body does not, the base picture of hover.
branches.cn: 飞鸟线：翅膀在动而身体不动，是 hover 最基础的画面。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: rotors and screen pointers copy the same held-still position.
branches.cn: 机械线：旋翼与屏幕指针复制了同样「停在一点」的位置。

branches.en: THE PERSON: lingering near a place is hovering done on the ground.
branches.cn: 人物线：在人身边或地点附近逗留，是地面版的悬停。

branches.en: THE THRESHOLD: something hangs just above a level or just before an event.
branches.cn: 临界线：事物悬在某个水平之上，或悬在事件发生之前。

branches.en: THE MIND: being between two choices is the inner version of the same balance.
branches.cn: 心理线：在两种选择之间，是同一平衡状态在心的内部的版本。

intro.en: Hover is a native verb with no affixes of its own; its family is made of English compounds such as hovercraft, hoverboard, and hoverfly.
intro.cn: hover 是本族动词，本身不带词缀；它的词族由 hovercraft、hoverboard、hoverfly 等英语复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: Hover has no Latin root, so the related forms below are English compounds and suffixes rather than Latin elements.
latinIntro.cn: hover 没有拉丁语词根，下面列出的相关词都是英语复合词与后缀，而不是拉丁语成分。

items.example: The oldest recorded form already means to stay still.
items.exampleCN: 最早有记录的词形已经表示「停着不动」。

items.meaning: to hang or rest in one place
items.example: Hoveren carries the still image into Middle English.
items.exampleCN: hoveren 把「停住」的画面带进中古英语。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms hovering.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 hovering。

items.example: The suffix -er forms hoverer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 hoverer。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms hovered.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 hovered。

items.example: Craft combines with hover to make hovercraft.
items.exampleCN: craft 与 hover 复合成 hovercraft。

items.meaning: a vehicle riding on a cushion of air
items.example: Hovercraft keeps the floating image in a vehicle.
items.exampleCN: hovercraft 把「浮着」的画面装进一种交通工具。

items.meaning: a board said to float above the ground
items.example: Hoverboard is a modern compound built on the same action.
items.exampleCN: hoverboard 是用同一动作造出的现代复合词。

items.meaning: a fly that stays still in the air
items.example: Hoverfly names an insect after its hovering flight.
items.exampleCN: hoverfly 用「悬停」的飞行方式为一种昆虫命名。

definition_zh: 喧闹声；嘈杂；骚动；鼓噪的混乱
definition_en: a loud mixture of many voices, or a noisy and confused scene of activity
core_image: 集市上一群人同时开口说话，声音混成一片，谁也听不清谁
scene: 菜市场里人挤人，讨价还价和叫卖声搅在一起，耳朵里只剩下一团吵闹。A hubbub of voices filled the crowded market hall from dawn to dusk.
sceneCN: 这里 hubbub 是「喧闹声；嘈杂的人声」（第 1 个义项：许多人同时说话造成的混杂响声）；句意：拥挤的菜市场大厅从早到晚都充满了嘈杂的人声。图中可辨识物件：菜市场、人群、摊位、混杂的叫喊。

collocations.zh: 在一片喧闹之上（大声说）

derivatives.zh: 由 hubbub 与 noise 构成的固定说法，义为「一片混杂的噪声」，把喧闹具体化为声源
与 hubbub 第二部分同形的拟声词，义为「咿呀地说；嘈杂地讲」，两者共享「含糊不清的说话声」画面
由 hubbub 加 -ous 构成的罕见形容词，义为「嘈杂的」，多见于十九世纪文人的仿古用法而非标准词典

senses.title: A loud confused mixture of voices
senses.definition: a continuous noise made by many people talking at the same time, so that no single voice can be understood
senses.definitionCN: 许多人同时说话形成的持续响声，结果谁也听不清谁在说什么
senses.example: A hubbub of laughter and talk rose from the dinner table.
senses.exampleCN: 餐桌上升起一片笑声和谈话交织的喧闹。
senses.why: The word imitates a blurred, bubbling sound, so the basic sense is many voices losing their edges in one another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词模仿的是模糊、像冒泡一样的声响，所以最基本的义项就是许多声音彼此糊成一片、失去边界的声响。

senses.title: A noisy confused scene
senses.definition: a busy, noisy place or crowd in which people and activities are mixed together
senses.definitionCN: 人多、声响杂、人或活动搅在一处的地方或场面
senses.example: The station was a hubbub of porters, whistles and rushing travellers.
senses.exampleCN: 车站里是一幅搬运工、哨声与赶车人搅在一起的嘈杂场面。
senses.why: Once a jumble of voices fills a place, the place itself is called a hubbub, so the sound names the scene that makes it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦混杂的人声充满某个地方，这个地方本身也被称为 hubbub，于是声音转而命名了发声的场面。

senses.title: Excited public uproar
senses.definition: the excited noise and activity of a crowd reacting to surprising news or a controversial event
senses.definitionCN: 人群对惊人消息或有争议事件作出的激动喧嚷与骚动
senses.example: The announcement set off a hubbub in the assembly hall.
senses.exampleCN: 这项宣布在礼堂里引起一片骚动。
senses.why: Excitement turns ordinary talk into a hubbub, so the word comes to name the noise of a crowd stirred by news rather than of routine chatter.
senses.whyCN: 激动把平常的交谈变成一片喧嚷，于是这个词开始指被消息搅动起来的人群之声，而不只是日常闲聊。

intro.en: Hubbub is a word of the sixteenth century made by copying a confused sound; Irish and Scots Gaelic have a word of similar shape meaning a war cry, but the usual view treats the English word as imitative, and the exact origin is not certain.
intro.cn: hubbub 是十六世纪出现的词，由模仿混乱的声音而来；爱尔兰语与苏格兰盖尔语里有一个形状相近、意为「战斗呐喊」的词，但通常认为英语这个词属拟声造词，确切来源并不确定。

items.en: Irish ubub is an exclamation of contempt or distress, and Scots Gaelic has ubub meaning a war cry; some link hubbub to these forms, but the link is a hypothesis, not an established etymology.
items.cn: 爱尔兰语中有表示轻蔑或惊恐的感叹词 ubub，苏格兰盖尔语有意为「战斗呐喊」的 ubub；有人认为 hubbub 与之相关，但这只是假说，并非定论。

items.en: Hubbub is recorded in English, usually in the form hububbe or hubbub, naming a confused noise or an outcry.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语中已记录 hububbe 或 hubbub 这样的拼写，指混乱的嘈杂声或众人呼喊。

items.en: The spelling settles on hubbub, and the word spreads from cries and riots to any noisy crowd.
items.cn: 十七世纪拼写稳定为 hubbub，词义也从呼喊与骚乱扩展到泛指喧闹的人群。

items.en: Writers often use the word the way it is used now, for the jumble of voices in markets, parliaments, and busy streets.
items.cn: 十八至十九世纪的作家开始像现在这样使用它：集市、议会与闹市中混杂的说话声。

items.en: Hubbub stays a lively newspaper and literary word for the background noise of crowds, and its origin remains uncertain.
items.cn: 现代英语里 hubbub 仍是报纸与文学中生动的词，用来写人群的背景噪声；它的来源至今仍不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built or sounding like hubbub through doubled syllables, and the near-meaning group collects the noise nouns it is often confused with.
note.cn: 形近组收通过叠音构成、或读音相近于 hubbub 的词；近义组收常与它混淆的各种「声音」名词。

entries.definition: The first half of a popcorn call; it only echoes the opening of hubbub and shares no root.
entries.definitionCN: 爆米花小贩吆喝的开头音节，与 hubbub 只是读音相近，词源无关；另注意 hubbub 的 b 常被误拼，中间要双写。

entries.definition: a low continuous sound of voices, made from a repeated syllable like hubbub
entries.definitionCN: 低而持续的人声，与 hubbub 一样靠重复音节造词

entries.definition: a loud commotion of voices and activity, a jollier sound-alike of hubbub
entries.definitionCN: 响亮的喧嚷与忙乱，读音与 hubbub 相近但更俏皮

entries.definition: a loud, unpleasant and continuous noise, not necessarily from voices
entries.definitionCN: 响亮刺耳、持续的噪声，未必来自人声

entries.definition: a loud and demanding noise, as of many people calling for something
entries.definitionCN: 喧闹而带要求的呼喊，多指众人齐声要求某事

entries.definition: a sudden noisy disturbance, closer to the uproar sense of hubbub
entries.definitionCN: 突然的嘈杂骚动，更接近 hubbub 的「鼓噪」义项

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the doubled syllables, the preposition patterns, and the unsettled origin recorded for hubbub.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子利用叠音音节、常见介词搭配，以及 hubbub 尚未定论的真实词源状况。

normal.en: Hub and bub, hub and bub: the two halves rock back and forth like many voices talking over each other.
normal.cn: hub 与 bub，hub 与 bub：两半来回摆动，就像许多声音互相压过对方。

normal.en: The middle b doubles, so hubbub is often misspelled with one b; remember two b in the middle and one at the end.
normal.cn: 词中的 b 要双写，所以 hubbub 常被误拼成一个 b；记住中间是两个 b，末尾是一个 b。

normal.en: Hubbub usually appears after a hubbub of, naming the voices, laughter or shouting that make it.
normal.cn: hubbub 常跟在 a hubbub of 之后，后面点出构成喧闹的人声、笑声或喊声。

normal.en: Records show hubbub first as a confused noise or an outcry, and the outcry sense survives in modern news writing.
normal.cn: 文献显示 hubbub 最初就指杂乱的响声或众人的呼喊，而「鼓噪」这层意思至今仍活跃在新闻报道中。

normal.en: The word is imitative, and possible Gaelic links are only a hypothesis, so do not treat them as its proven origin.
normal.cn: 这个词属拟声造词，与盖尔语的联系只是假说，所以不要把假说当成已证实的词源。

abstract.en: Picture a crowded noodle stand at noon: every customer speaks at once and the words melt into one warm blur.
abstract.cn: 想象中午拥挤的面摊：每个客人都同时开口，话语熔成一片暖烘烘的模糊。

abstract.en: Picture the same crowd with the words gone and only the mix left, like an orchestra tuning before a concert.
abstract.cn: 想象同样那群人，话语被抹去，只剩混杂的声响，像音乐会开场前的调音。

abstract.en: Picture a hush falling as a speaker steps up, and the hubbub becomes the sound of expectation.
abstract.cn: 想象发言者上台时全场安静下来，那片喧嚷其实正是期待的声音。

examples.en: A hubbub of laughter rose from the playground.
examples.cn: 操场上响起一片笑声交织的喧闹。

examples.en: She could barely hear him above the hubbub.
examples.cn: 在一片喧闹声中，她几乎听不见他说话。

examples.en: Reporters made a hubbub around the new champion.
examples.cn: 记者们在新冠军周围引起一阵喧嚷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈巴巴」——菜市场里此起彼伏的喊声，连起来就是哈巴巴、哈巴巴；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为由模仿混乱的人声而来（拟声造词），十六世纪英语首见，拼作 hububbe 或 hubbub；是否与爱尔兰语、苏格兰盖尔语的感叹词 ubub 有关尚属不确定；核心义「许多声音混成一片、听不清的噪声」。

sensesIntro.en: Hubbub starts as a blurred mass of voices, then names the noisy scene that produces them, and finally the excited noise of a crowd stirred by news.
sensesIntro.cn: hubbub 先指混成一片、听不清的人声，再指制造这种声音的嘈杂场面，最后指人群被消息搅动而发出的鼓噪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd talking at once in a market, voices merging into one blur.
core.cn: 核心意象：集市里一群人同时开口，声音糊成一片。

branches.en: THE SOUND: many voices lose their edges, which is the first recorded sense.
branches.cn: 声音线：许多声音失去边界，这是最早记录下来的义项。

branches.en: THE SCENE: a place is named by the noise that fills it.
branches.cn: 场面线：一个地方以填满它的噪声来命名。

branches.en: THE UPROAR: excitement and news lift ordinary talk into a hubbub.
branches.cn: 鼓噪线：激动与消息把平常的闲聊抬升成一片鼓噪。

branches.en: Both senses share the jumble, one heard and one seen.
branches.cn: 这两个义项共享「混杂」这一特征，一个落在听觉上，一个落在视觉上。

branches.en: A crowded noisy hall and a startled crowd are the same picture at different levels.
branches.cn: 拥挤闹哄的会场和被惊动的人群，是同一幅画面在不同尺度上的呈现。

intro.en: Hubbub has no prefix or suffix; it is a reduplicated imitative word, and its family is made of other noise words rather than of affixed forms.
intro.cn: hubbub 没有前缀或后缀，它是叠音的拟声词；它的词族由其他表示噪声的词构成，而不是加词缀的派生形式。

latinIntro.en: Hubbub has no Latin or Greek root, and the possible Gaelic links are a hypothesis, so no Latin family is given
latinIntro.cn: hubbub 没有拉丁语或希腊语词根，与盖尔语的可能联系也只是假说，因此不列出拉丁同源词

items.example: Hububbe is one of the earliest recorded spellings.
items.exampleCN: hububbe 是最早见于记录的一种拼写。

items.example: Hubbub keeps the doubling of the syllables.
items.exampleCN: hubbub 保留了音节的重复结构。

items.example: The plural -s forms hubbubs.
items.exampleCN: 复数词尾 -s 构成 hubbubs。

items.example: Hub is the opening beat of the noise.
items.exampleCN: hub 是这声噪声的第一拍。

items.meaning: the echoing close of the word
items.example: Bub repeats and echoes the first beat.
items.exampleCN: bub 回应并重复第一拍。

items.example: Murmur shares the reduplicated shape.
items.exampleCN: murmur 共用这种叠音结构。

items.meaning: to talk in a confused way
items.example: Babble keeps the bubbling sound idea.
items.exampleCN: babble 保留了那种冒泡般的声音意象。

items.example: Hullabaloo is a jollier cousin of the hubbub family.
items.exampleCN: hullabaloo 是这类喧闹词里更俏皮的一员。

definition_zh: 挤作一团；挤成一团站着；缩成一团；暗中商议；拥挤的人群；（美式橄榄球）队员围圈；拥挤杂乱的一堆
definition_en: to crowd closely together, especially for warmth, safety or private conversation; also the tight group or heap so formed
core_image: 寒夜里几个人弯着腰挤成一团，肩背贴着肩背，围成一个小小的圆
scene: 沙漠的夜晚冷得刺骨，赶驼人裹紧了衣服，背靠背挤在一起取暖。The travellers huddle around the fire as the desert night turns cold.
sceneCN: 这里 huddle 是「挤作一团」（第 1 个义项：为取暖或安全感而紧紧挤在一起）；句意：沙漠的夜晚转冷，旅人们挤在篝火边取暖。画面重点：弯下的背脊、贴近的肩膀、围成的小小一圈。

pos.zh: 挤作一团；蜷缩；暗中聚在一起商议
挤在一起的一群；杂乱的一堆；（美式橄榄球）队员围圈

collocations.zh: 挤成一团；紧紧靠在一起

derivatives.zh: huddle 加 -ed 作形容词，指「蜷缩着的、挤在一起的」，如 huddled figures 蜷缩的身影
huddle 加表人的后缀 -er，指挤在一起的人，较少使用
huddle 加 -ing 作名词，指挤作一团、围聚商议的行为

senses.title: To press closely together for warmth
senses.definition: to crowd close together, often bending low, in order to keep warm or feel safe
senses.definitionCN: 为了取暖或获得安全感而紧紧挤在一起，常常弯着身子
senses.example: The children huddled together under the thin blanket.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在薄毯子下挤作一团。
senses.why: The oldest image of the word is bodies pressed into a low, tight mass, and warmth is the reason people form that mass.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的画面就是身体压成一个又低又紧的团，而取暖正是人们愿意挤成这个团的原因；所以「挤」和「暖」从一开始就绑在一起。

senses.title: To curl up small
senses.definition: to draw the body into a small, rounded shape, as from cold, fear or pain
senses.definitionCN: 因寒冷、恐惧或疼痛而把身体缩成小而圆的形状
senses.example: She huddled in the corner with her coat pulled round her.
senses.exampleCN: 她把外套裹紧，蜷缩在角落里。
senses.why: When one person does the pressing alone, the group image shrinks into a single body folded up small against the cold.
senses.whyCN: 当「挤」的动作落到一个人身上，本来一群人压成的团就缩小成一个独自对抗寒冷的身体，于是 huddle 转指「蜷缩」。

senses.title: To gather in a close group
senses.definition: to come together in a close group, for example to talk or to wait
senses.definitionCN: 聚拢成一个紧密的小群体，例如交谈或等待
senses.example: Reporters huddled around the coach after the match.
senses.exampleCN: 赛后记者们挤在教练周围。
senses.why: Warmth is not the only reason people bunch up; curiosity and waiting produce the same tight circle, so the verb widens to any close gathering.
senses.whyCN: 人们挤成一团的理由不止取暖，好奇与等待也会造出同样紧密的圆圈，因此这个动词扩展为「任何紧密的聚集」。

senses.title: To talk secretly in a group
senses.definition: to crowd together in order to discuss something privately, away from other people
senses.definitionCN: 挤在一起私下讨论某事，避开旁人
senses.example: The managers huddled to decide who would speak first.
senses.exampleCN: 经理们凑在一起商议由谁先发言。
senses.why: Heads brought close together make speech hard for outsiders to hear, so the physical circle becomes a sheltered space for private talk.
senses.whyCN: 头挨得越近，外人越听不清说话内容，因此身体围成的这个圈自然成了屏蔽旁人的私密谈话空间。

senses.title: A crowd squeezed together
senses.definition: a small group of people pressed close together under one blanket or in one place
senses.definitionCN: 一小群人一起盖一条毯子或同处一地而紧紧挤在一起
senses.example: A huddle of students waited outside the library door.
senses.exampleCN: 一群学生挤在图书馆门口等候。
senses.why: Because huddling is so common, the crowd itself is called a huddle, and the verb quietly becomes a noun for the lump of bodies.
senses.whyCN: 挤在一起太常见了，于是这群人本身就被叫作一个 huddle，动词悄悄转成名词，专指那一坨挤在一起的身体。

senses.title: A circle of players
senses.definition: the circle of players who gather to hear the next play during an American football game
senses.definitionCN: 美式橄榄球比赛中球员聚成一圈，听教练或队长布置下一档战术
senses.example: The quarterback called the play in the huddle.
senses.exampleCN: 四分卫在队员围圈时喊出了战术。
senses.why: Football players keep the opposing side from hearing the plan by bending into a closed ring, which is exactly the sheltered circle of sense four.
senses.whyCN: 橄榄球球员弯下腰围成一个封闭的圈，好让对手听不见计划，这与第 4 个义项里那个屏蔽旁人的圈完全一致，只是场合更专业。

senses.title: A jumbled heap
senses.definition: a confused heap or mass of things crowded together without order
senses.definitionCN: 杂乱无章地挤在一起的堆、团
senses.example: A huddle of old chairs blocked the back steps.
senses.exampleCN: 一堆旧椅子乱挤在后门台阶上。
senses.why: Anything pressed into a shapeless mass looks like the bodies in the core picture, so the word transfers from people to objects and to crowds of buildings.
senses.whyCN: 任何被压成无定形的一团的东西，看上去都像核心意象里那些挤在一起的身体，所以这个词从人扩展到物，甚至扩展到一片拥挤的房子。

intro.en: Huddle comes from Germanic roots meaning to hide or to heap up, and it was first a verb of concealment before it became a word about crowded bodies.
intro.cn: huddle 的词根来自日耳曼语，本义与「藏起来、堆起来」有关，最初是表示遮盖的动词，后来才转指挤在一起的人。

items.en: The verb is generally traced to Germanic bases for hiding or heaping, with a likely diminutive ending.
items.cn: 一般认为这个动词追溯至日耳曼语中表示「藏匿、堆积」的词根，并带有一个指小的后缀。

items.en: Compare Flemish and Dutch huddeen, to hide or shelter, often given as a close relative.
items.cn: 可比较佛兰芒语与荷兰语的 huddeen（隐藏、庇护），词典多把它视为近亲。

items.en: Huddle first appears in English in the sixteenth century meaning to hide or to cover up.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语里首次出现 huddle，当时意为隐藏或遮盖。

items.en: Writers use it for heaping things in a confused mass, and for people crowding close.
items.cn: 十七世纪的作家用它表示把东西胡乱堆成一团，也用于描述人群挤在一起。

items.en: The noun for a crowded group becomes common, and team sports later adopt it for the players circle.
items.cn: 十九世纪表示拥挤人群的名词用法开始流行，体育比赛后来又借它命名球员围成的圈。

note.en: Huddle belongs to a family of crowding words, and it is often confused in spelling with the hue of colours and with muggle-like forms.
note.cn: huddle 属于表示「拥挤、聚拢」的一组词，拼写上容易与表示色彩的 hue、以及近似 muggle 的形状混淆。

entries.definition: past form and adjective meaning squeezed close together
entries.definitionCN: huddle 的过去式与形容词，指挤在一起的、蜷缩着的

entries.definition: to curl up or press together closely
entries.definitionCN: 蜷缩起来；紧紧挤在一起

entries.definition: a light frame to jump over in a race, or an obstacle
entries.definitionCN: 跨栏；障碍；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to hold someone close affectionately
entries.definitionCN: 亲昵地搂抱，带感情色彩

entries.definition: to form a small close group
entries.definitionCN: （使）聚集成小团，多用于物

entries.definition: to settle close for warmth
entries.definitionCN: 舒服地依偎在一起取暖

normalIntro.en: Huddle is a heap of bodies: people pressed low and close because of cold, fear or a secret.
normalIntro.cn: huddle 是一团身体堆在一起：因为寒冷、害怕或要说悄悄话，人们压低身子挤近。

normal.en: Huddle together is the most common pattern, as in children huddled together.
normal.cn: huddle together 是最常见的搭配，如孩子们挤作一团。

normal.en: Huddle up adds the thought of curling into a ball.
normal.cn: huddle up 多了一层「蜷成一个球」的意思。

normal.en: The -le ending suggests a small repeated movement, like the folding of arms and knees.
normal.cn: -le 结尾常带「小而反复」的感觉，正像手臂和膝盖一阵阵收拢。

normal.en: The noun huddle names the circle itself, as in a huddle of reporters.
normal.cn: 名词 huddle 指那个圈本身，如记者们围成的一圈。

normal.en: Compare cluster for things and crowd for large numbers; huddle keeps a feeling of cold or secrecy.
normal.cn: 对比 cluster（多指物）和 crowd（指大群人数），huddle 保留着寒意或秘密的意味。

abstract.en: Picture a knot of people bent low under one blanket at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时分一群人弓着身子，合盖一条毯子，挤成一团。

abstract.en: See a child folded up in a doorway against the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子顶住风，蜷缩在门洞里。

abstract.en: See heads leaning into one tight circle, voices kept low.
abstract.cn: 想象几颗头凑成一个紧圆的圈，说话声压得很低。

examples.en: The hikers huddled in a hut until the storm passed.
examples.cn: 徒步的人挤在小屋里，直到暴风雨过去。

examples.en: The team got into a huddle before the last minute of the match.
examples.cn: 比赛最后一分钟前，队员们围成一圈。

examples.en: In the cold station, a huddle of passengers waited for the last train.
examples.cn: 寒冷的车站里，一群乘客挤在一起等末班车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈斗」——冻得哈着气、斗在一起挤紧：挤作一团取暖。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源一般认为追溯至日耳曼语中表示「藏匿、堆积」的词根，带指小后缀 -le，可比较佛兰芒语与荷兰语的 huddeen（隐藏、庇护）；十六世纪进入英语，本义藏匿，后转指人挤成一团。这个词不是来自拉丁语，拉丁语里没有直接对应词。

sensesIntro.en: Huddle starts with bodies pressed together for warmth, narrows to one body curled up, widens to any close gathering, and ends as the name of the circle or heap itself.
sensesIntro.cn: huddle 从为取暖而挤在一起的身体开始，收窄到一个人蜷缩，再扩展到任何紧密的聚集，最后转成名词，指那个圈或那一堆本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few figures bent low and pressed shoulder to shoulder in the cold.
core.cn: 核心意象：寒夜里几个人压低身子、肩贴肩挤成一团。

branches.en: Pressing together for warmth is the everyday body sense.
branches.cn: 为取暖而挤在一起是日常的身体义项。

branches.en: One body folded up takes the same shape.
branches.cn: 一个人的蜷缩与一群人的挤压是同一种形状。

branches.en: Any closely gathered people form the same tight ring.
branches.cn: 任何紧密聚拢的人都形成同样的紧圈。

branches.en: A tight ring shuts others out, so it becomes a place for private play calls.
branches.cn: 紧圈把旁人隔在外，于是成了私下商议或布置战术的地方。

branches.en: The mass of bodies turns into a noun for the group and for any crowded heap.
branches.cn: 成团的身体转成名词，指这群人以及任何拥挤的一堆。

intro.en: Huddle has no Latin parts; its family grows through the old diminutive ending and through compounding and phrasal use.
intro.cn: huddle 没有拉丁语构件，它的词族靠古老的指小词尾与复合、短语用法扩展。

latinIntro.en: Huddle has no secure Latin ancestor; the Latin entries here are given only for comparison with English crowding verbs.
latinIntro.cn: huddle 没有可靠的拉丁语祖先，这里列出的拉丁词仅用于与英语「拥挤」类动词对照。

items.example: The flock huddles against the wind.
items.exampleCN: 羊群顶着风挤在一起。

items.example: They huddled under the awning.
items.exampleCN: 他们在雨棚下挤作一团。

items.example: Huddling kept the calves warm.
items.exampleCN: 挤在一起让牛犊暖和起来。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作细小或反复的词尾
items.example: The ending -le marks a small repeated motion.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -le 标记细小而反复的动作。

items.example: The boy huddled up in his sleeping bag.
items.exampleCN: 男孩蜷缩进睡袋里。

items.meaning: an old name for a private meeting place
items.meaningCN: 古旧说法，指私下碰头的房间
items.example: Huddle-room appears in older writings.
items.exampleCN: huddle-room 见于较早的文献。

items.example: A huddle of umbrellas waited at the stop.
items.exampleCN: 站台上聚着一堆雨伞。
